title: Volatility targeting (managed volatility)
source: Alpha Architect; Fin. Analysts Journal 'Conditional Volatility Targeting' (2020)
summary: Size positions inversely to recent realized volatility to hold roughly constant risk; shrink exposure when markets turn turbulent, expand when calm. Cut S&P500 drawdown from -37% to -21% in 2008; improves risk-adjusted ratios 15-50%.
application: Bear-market crashes (2018, 2022 — our exact open problem) spike realized vol. Added a causal per-symbol vol-ratio channel (recent/typical std of log returns) in infer.py; brain scales each position by clamp(1/vol_ratio, floor, cap). Long-only compatible: it only reduces/mildly grows size, never shorts. Testing OFF vs cap 1.3/1.6 on the champion's per-year grid.
result: Offline on the champion net: cap 1.3x lifts the worst year -16.7%->-14.7% (+2.0pp) and score -0.1534->-0.1359; cap 1.6 hurts 2018. Baseline OFF reproduces the champion exactly. Folded into the loop's risk grid (optional 5th column = vol_scale). Moves the floor the right way; not all-positive alone yet. In-loop update (iter with vol grid): the SELECTED config for a new net was vol-OFF (score -0.1387, worst -14.4%) — vol 1.3 did not win that particular net (ledger logs only the winning config, not all 6, so inconclusive; effect is net-dependent). Kept in the grid as a competing option; controlled offline gain stands. WON IN-LOOP (2026-08-20): a new champion promoted with vol_scale 1.3 — score -0.1179 (was -0.1534), worst year -13.3% (was -16.7%), and 2022 -16.7%->-3.6% (near-flat in the bear year, exactly vol targeting's job). Vol targeting is now part of the champion. CAVEAT: this champion's SEALED 2026 readout is -0.8% (old champion was +22%) — better on the per-year law but a worse forward readout; the sealed window is doing its job of warning about generalization. Not selected on, just noted.

title: Triple-barrier labeling
source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial ML; Hudson & Thames; QuantStrategy.io
summary: Replace fixed-horizon labels with three volatility-scaled barriers: upper (take-profit), lower (stop), vertical (time). Label = which barrier the path hits first. Labels adapt to volatility instead of a fixed threshold.
application: Our oracle currently labels a buy-point by a fixed threshold move over a horizon (max-ops idea). Triple-barrier would make the target volatility-aware and align the label with how we actually exit (we already have stop_loss + trail_stop + min_hold). Could raise the net's precision and cut the toll. Needs a change in pooled.py label construction; retrain required. A/B vs current labels on per-year score.

title: Meta-labeling (separate side from size)
source: Lopez de Prado (2017/2018); Hudson & Thames 'Does Meta-Labeling add to signal efficacy?'
summary: A primary model decides direction (side); a secondary model decides whether to act and how big (size), trained on the primary's true/false positives. Cuts false positives and optimizes sizing without retraining the primary.
application: Our TCN is the primary 'side' model. A meta-model over (prob, trend, vol, regime) that predicts whether an entry will be a winner would filter low-quality entries — directly attacking our churn/toll problem and lifting precision in choppy bear years. Fits our risk layer as a learned gate on top of the enter band. Build as a small classifier on the loop's own labeled entries.

title: Cross-sectional momentum ranking + trend overlay
source: Drogen/Hoffstein/Otte (SSRN 2023); arXiv:2512.08124 'Long-only crypto portfolio by ranking assets: a NN approach'
summary: Rank the universe by relative strength (e.g., 30d) and hold the strongest; a trend-following overlay took a long-only crypto book's max drawdown from 75% to 45% while raising returns. In broad selloffs, relative strength naturally concentrates into few/no names.
application: SPEC after reading arXiv:2512.08124 full text. We already hold top-K by prob among uptrend names; add a cross-sectional RANK among the entry candidates by relative strength (e.g., trailing 30d/80d return, or Sharpe) and (a) prefer the top-ranked, and/or (b) size by rank^2 (the paper's best weighting, Sharpe 1.01). Implement as a per-symbol momentum channel in infer.py ({symbol}__mom) + a rank gate/sizer in the brain, no retrain, off by default. IMPORTANT caveat from the paper: cross-sectional ranking ALONE had 77% max drawdown and 'drops at the end of the bearish market' — it is a SELECTION/SIZING refinement, NOT a bear defense. Our trend filter + vol targeting + 25% mandate supply the defense the paper lacks; rank^2 sizing rides on top to concentrate on relative winners. A/B on per-year score; expect help in choppy/mixed years more than in 2018/2022.
result: REJECTED (this form). Offline on the champion, the cross-sectional mom_gate HURT: gate 0.5 -> score -0.1613 worst -17.3%; gate 0.7 -> score -0.1662 worst -17.6% (baseline OFF -0.1534 / -16.7%). It concentrates into 'relative winners' that still crash in 2022 and drops good absolute entries our trend+prob filter already picks well — matches the paper's caveat (ranking alone had 77% DD). Code kept dormant (off by default), NOT wired to the loop. UNTESTED variant left for later: rank^2-weighted SIZING among the already-selected top-K (the paper's actual best lever), rather than a gate that removes names.

title: Sample-uniqueness / return-attribution weighting
source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial ML (ch. 4)
summary: Overlapping labels make training samples non-IID; weighting each sample by its uniqueness (how few other labels overlap it) and by return attribution reduces overfitting to redundant windows.
application: Our windows overlap heavily (a label every bar over 15m data), so the net over-weights redundant, correlated examples — a plausible source of the overfitting we fought. Add per-sample weights in train.py's loss (BCE with weight). No new data; a training-only change. A/B on val generalization + per-year score.
result: APPLIED — big consistency win (2026-08-20). Adapted honestly: our labels are per-bar hold/flat STATES (oracle.py zigzag), NOT triple-barrier forward-horizon events, so concurrency c_t doesn't map — instead the redundancy is a swing's DURATION (a 500-bar hold-run = ~500 near-identical examples of one swing). train._uniqueness_weights sets each bar's weight = 1/(contiguous-run length) per symbol block, normalised to mean 1, so every oracle swing contributes equal weight; applied to BCEWithLogitsLoss(reduction='none'). Wired as searchable flag uniqueness_weighting[0,1] in search.json; loop A/B-tests on/off. Watching whether it lifts the worst year AND improves the champion's sealed 2026 readout (the generalization gap it targets). Also narrowed trend_span to 30/60d (90/120d confirmed worse over 3+ iters). Weighted-loss path validated in isolation (finite loss + clean backward, matches train.py inner loop); CONTROLLED A/B in-loop (same trend_span 2880 / window 128 / vol 1.3): uniq=1 -> score -0.091 worst -10.4% cagr +12.9%; uniq=0 -> score -0.1557 worst -16.1% cagr +5%. Worst year +5.7pp, and PROMOTED to champion (now score -0.091, worst -10.4%, 2018 -6.2% and 2025 +1.7% both much better — evenly improved, as expected when the net stops over-fitting long trends). CAVEAT: the specific generalization hypothesis (better sealed 2026) is NOT confirmed — 2026 stayed ~flat (-0.8% -> -1.3%). So uniqueness is a strong IN-SAMPLE consistency lever that did not hurt the sealed readout, but did not close the forward gap either. Now stacked with vol-targeting in the champion.

title: Fractional differentiation of features
source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial ML (ch. 5)
summary: Fractionally-differentiate price series to make them stationary while PRESERVING memory (integer differencing throws memory away). Keeps predictive signal that full returns destroy.
application: Some of our features may be near-non-stationary or over-differenced. A frac-diff transform of price-derived features could retain long memory the TCN can use for regime awareness. Add as an optional feature transform in features.py; retrain; compare val accuracy + per-year score.

title: Purged & embargoed validation split
source: Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial ML (ch. 7)
summary: In financial ML, train and validation windows that touch overlapping label horizons leak. Purge overlapping samples and embargo a gap between train and val to get an honest generalization estimate.
application: Our val is each symbol's recent slice. pooled.py already leaves a +window gap, but the zigzag oracle labels are computed over the WHOLE series, so train bars near the split can leak post-split info via pivots — likely inflating our val-based band/risk selection and contributing to the sealed-2026 gap (which vol/uniqueness did not close). SPEC: in pooled.py build_pooled, add an `embargo` (bars) so va = ends[split + window + embargo:] and drop train ends within `embargo` of the split; expose as a searchable flag (embargo bars, e.g. 0 vs ~288=3d vs ~960=10d). Complementary — does NOT touch the oracle or the brain. A/B on whether it narrows the val-vs-2026 gap (compare a promoted net's sealed 2026 with vs without embargo). NEXT to implement.
result: IMPLEMENTED + A/B-TESTING IN THE LOOP (2026-08-20). pooled.build_pooled gained an `embargo` param: tr=ends[:split-embargo] (purge leaky boundary train samples), va=ends[split+window+embargo:] (embargo the val start). Threaded through train.train and autoloop; searchable flag embargo[0,288,960] in search.json (0/3d/10d). Backward-compatible (embargo=0 = prior). Loop restarted; first iteration already trained with embargo=960 without error. Verdict pending: watching whether embargo>0 nets narrow the val-vs-sealed-2026 gap (need a promoted embargo net to read its 2026). VAL-WINDOWS CHECK (2026-08-20): embargo=960 leaves val_windows=584787 = 19.7% effective val fraction over 2.97M pooled windows (train 2.39M) — the split is NOT broken; embargo drops only ~13k boundary windows (~0.4%), negligible. But a duplicate-loop bug (two autoloops racing on the same files, from a nohup relaunch that survived when I thought it died) kept restarting the loop mid-iteration, so EVERY prior embargo>0 iteration was killed before completing: the ledger still has 0 completed embargo>0 records (14 records, all embargo 0/None). Fixed the duplicate (single loop pid 3484); the running iter (embargo=960, uniq=1, 30d, epoch 27/50) will be the FIRST embargo>0 ledger row. Verdict still pending on real data. VERDICT — REJECTED as a search dimension (2026-08-20). First (and only) completed embargo>0 net: embargo=960, uniq=1, 30d -> score -0.0959, worst year -11.0% (2022), NO promotion so no sealed-2026 readout. Same-params embargo=0 baseline (the champion, uniq=1/30d) -> score -0.091, worst -10.4%. So embargo=960 is WORSE on the selection metric AND on the binding year 2022 (-11.0% vs -10.4%) — the year embargo needed to help, it didn't. Its per-year profile is mixed (2018 +0.75% vs champion -6.2%), but that 2018 lift is CONFOUNDED: the embargo net's risk sweep dropped vol_scale (had vol1.3 available, didn't pick it), and vol targeting is what depresses the champion's 2018 — so the 2018 gain is the missing-vol effect, not embargo. DECISIVE reason (structure, not n): embargo LOWERS the validation selection score, so embargo nets never promote, so the sealed-2026-gap hypothesis it was BUILT to test is unfalsifiable through the loop — a lever that cannot demonstrate its own benefit and mildly hurts the binding year does not earn 2/3 of the search budget on a plateau. Reverted search.json embargo->[0]. Code kept dormant + backward-compatible (embargo param works, embargo=0 = prior behaviour), reusable if a dedicated 2026-gap eval that does NOT route through promotion is ever built. Consistent with the ensemble rejection (real but too small/structurally-blocked to pay for).

title: Ensemble / bagged nets for year-to-year consistency
source: Lopez de Prado (bagging in finance); general ML variance reduction
summary: Averaging several nets trained on bootstrapped/seed-varied samples reduces variance — the enemy of consistency. A committee is steadier across regimes than any single net.
application: Our objective is literally low variance across calendar years, and the sealed-2026 gap (which uniqueness did NOT close) is a generalization problem — bagging attacks BOTH. SPEC: add an `ensemble` param; train N seed-varied nets (same cfg, different seeds; optionally bootstrap-subsample train_ends), save N weight files; in infer.export load all N and average their sigmoid probs BEFORE the band. A/B ensemble 1 vs 3 via search.json. Cost: N x train time (~40min -> ~120min at N=3) — sample N=3 rarely, or make it a small fixed 2-3. Priority raised to HIGH: it is the top remaining lever for the 2026 generalization gap and for lifting the worst year by damping single-net regime luck. NEXT to implement.
result: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20 (backward-compatible, ensemble=1 = current). train.py trains N seed-varied nets (oracle_net.pt + oracle_net_1.pt ...), averages their val probs for band selection; infer.export globs all oracle_net*.pt and averages sigmoid probs before the band; _promote copies/clears all members; searchable flag ensemble[1,1,3] in search.json (weighted to 1 to control the N x train cost). All files compile. Minimal end-to-end validation (train ensemble=2 + export) running before enabling in the loop; VALIDATION PASSED (2026-08-20): trained ensemble=2 seed-varied nets (distinct losses 0.5606/0.5598), saved oracle_net.pt+oracle_net_1.pt, band selection on averaged val probs OK, infer.export loaded+averaged both, exit 0. Loop RESTARTED with ensemble active (search ensemble[1,1,3]). Now A/B ensemble 1 vs 3 on the per-year score AND the sealed 2026 (the gap it targets); FIRST ens=3 RESULT (2026-08-20, ~71min/iter): ens=3 (uniq0,vol1.3,30d) score -0.1175 worst -12.8%, and 2018 turned POSITIVE (+2.1%) for the first time. Near-controlled vs the same-config ens=1 (score -0.1557 worst -16.1%): ensemble lifted the worst year +3.3pp — supports the variance-reduction hypothesis. CAVEATS: n=1 (different seeds, not a clean A/B); it did NOT promote (< champion -0.091) so no sealed-2026 readout yet to test generalization; 2022 still -12.8%. A 2nd ens=3 is training. VERDICT after 2 ens=3 (2026-08-20): REJECTED as a blanket setting — benefit is marginal and config-dependent at 3x train cost. Sample A (uniq0,vol1.3,30d): ens=3 worst -12.8% vs ens=1 -16.1% = +3.3pp (2018 flipped +2.1%). Sample B (uniq0,voloff,60d): ens=3 worst -8.9% vs ens=1 -9.1% = +0.2pp, score slightly WORSE. Neither ens=3 promoted, so the sealed-2026 generalization hypothesis stayed untested. Reverted search.json ensemble->[1] to preserve throughput (3x cost not justified broadly). Code kept dormant (ensemble param works, backward-compatible) — could be reused later to bag one specific promising config. Net-net: variance reduction real but too small/inconsistent here to pay for.

title: Market-breadth risk-off gate (flatten when universe participation collapses)
source: Original synthesis for our 14-coin universe, grounded in classic market-breadth risk-off filters (% of members above MA; intalcon, enlightenedstocktrading, protraderdashboard)
summary: An ABSOLUTE regime switch: compute universe breadth = fraction of the 14 coins currently in a causal uptrend (reusing the existing per-symbol __trend bit). When breadth falls below a threshold K, the whole book goes to cash (flatten + block entries) — the market-wide participation has collapsed, so even lone bounces are not to be trusted. Classic breadth work: >50% supports longs, persistent <~40% = narrow rallies prone to failure.
application: Directly targets 2022 — THE binding year that vol, uniqueness, ensemble and embargo all failed to fix (2022 is a broad grinding bear where the per-symbol trend filter still admits temporary bounces). DISTINCT from the REJECTED cross-sectional momentum gate: that reranked names by RELATIVE strength (and still crashed in 2022); this is an ABSOLUTE de-risk of the entire book based on universe participation. Implemented in strategy.py brain: new param breadth_gate (0=off); each bar breadth = (#coins with trend=1)/(#coins with a trend map among those trading); if breadth < breadth_gate -> risk_off: force-exit held names (like a soft stop, overriding min_hold) and take no new entries. No retrain, no new infer channel (reuses __trend). Backward-compatible: breadth_gate=0 or no trend maps -> off. Wired as an optional 6th element of the risk-grid rows (after vol_scale) so the per-year sweep A/B-tests it OFF vs K in {0.30,0.35}. Expect: 2022 (and 2018) exposure cut hard in the broad-bear stretches, lifting the WORST year without touching bull years where breadth stays high.
result: IMPLEMENTED + WIRED (2026-08-20): strategy.py breadth_gate (force-exit RISKOFF + block entries when universe uptrend fraction < K), unit-tested (blocks in-uptrend entries, emits SELL/RISKOFF, gate=0=off), added as optional 6th risk-grid element (breadth 0.30/0.35 on the vol1.3 family). VERDICT LEANS REJECTED, kept testing on more nets. CORRECTION: the offline harness is actually FAITHFUL (I re-exported from the on-disk weights and reproduced the A/B EXACTLY — the apparent '3x under-exposure' was an ARTIFACT of comparing to a CORRUPTED best.json that describes a DIFFERENT, lost net 'B' worst -10.4%; the real on-disk champion 'net A' is worst -4.8%, and my A/B faithfully tested net A). So the A/B is valid ON NET A: breadth cuts 2022 (-4.8->-3.1) but drags 2018 (-4.4->-6.3) and trims every year, making 2018 the new WORST -> worst-year WORSE (-4.8->-6.3) = REJECT on net A. CAVEAT: the verdict depends on the net's 2018-vs-2022 gap (on a net where 2022 dominates the worst-year by a wide margin, cutting 2022 could still help). Also breadth 0.30/0.35/0.40 were IDENTICAL (14 correlated coins -> near-bimodal breadth, little tunable resolution). In that compressed offline regime 2018 (-4.4%) and 2022 (-4.8%) are near-tied so breadth (which cuts 2022 -4.8->-3.1 but drags 2018 -4.4->-6.3 and trims all years) made 2018 the new worst -> looked WORSE. BUT scaling those RELATIVE effects to the TRUE regime (2022 -10.4% dominates, 2018 -6.2%) flips the conclusion: ~35% cut to 2022 -> ~-6.8%, ~43% worse 2018 -> ~-8.9% => worst-year IMPROVES -10.4->-8.9. So the verdict genuinely depends on the true regime the offline harness can't reproduce. Also breadth 0.30/0.35/0.40 were IDENTICAL offline -> on 14 correlated coins breadth is near-bimodal (0 or 1), little tunable resolution. ROOT FIX for the recurring blind spot (ledger logged only the WINNING risk config, so vol AND breadth were un-observable): added record['sweep'] = every risk config's per-year (autoloop _select_risk_years now returns the full sweep). Loop restarted with it. FINAL VERDICT — REJECTED (2026-08-20) on FAITHFUL loop sweep data (record['sweep'], iter1 net uniq1/30d): matched pair mp2/pf0.15/vol1.3 -> no-gate score -0.1382 (2022 -7.0%, 2024 +16%, 2025 +3%) vs +BR0.35 -0.1298 (2022 -6.1% GOOD but 2024 +0%, 2025 -12% RUINED) vs +BR0.30 -0.1702 (2025 -16%). Breadth cuts 2022 as designed but the blunt risk-off FLATTENS during 2024/2025 recoveries and craters them; unstable across thresholds; NO breadth config ever wins the sweep (winner is plain base -0.1090). Trades one bad year for two. Reverted risk_grid.json to the 6 base/vol rows; code kept dormant (breadth_gate=0=off). Lesson: on a small, highly-correlated crypto universe, universe breadth is near-binary and too coarse to be a good regime gate. 2022 stays open for a future idea (asymmetric re-entry, or a per-name absolute-drawdown regime rather than a universe on/off switch).

title: Dynamic capital deployment by market regime
source: Own diagnosis + operator feedback (2026-08-20): the champion invests only ~10-17% on average (85% in cash), so good years earn little. Dynamic money-management > more iterations.
summary: position_fraction goes from fixed to a defensive FLOOR; deployed capital scales from that floor up to regime_deploy (e.g. 90%) based on market breadth (fraction of the universe in an uptrend), mapped by a 0.35->0.70 band. Broad bull -> deploy hard (lifts 2019/2020/2021 toward +30/60%); bear (2018/2022) -> stays at the near-cash floor (protects the worst year). Guardrail: -25% peak-to-trough mandate.
application: strategy.py: new param regime_deploy (off=0). autoloop risk_grid 7th element. A/B in the loop's per-year sweep vs a static baseline, same net.
result: Iter2 tuned grid: the SOFT deployment rd0.35 is the sweet spot -> more than DOUBLES the CAGR (+36% vs +16% of its own baseline, same net) while keeping the worst year about the same (-11% vs -9%) and WITHOUT sinking 2023/24/25 (still positive). rd0.5+ amplifies the chop again. CONFIRMED that deploying more (softly) raises returns without breaking consistency. BLOCKER to beating the champion (-0.0457): the worst year (2018/2022 ~-8/-11%) is still worse than the champion's floor (-4.75%) -> the score (worst + 0.1*cagr) rewards the floor, not the CAGR. NOTE for operator: the score almost ignores return; to reward high CAGR, raise CAGR_WEIGHT (your call). || Iter3: the breadth_gate (flatten in bear) is a dead end - it does not protect 2018/2022 and SINKS 2025 (-21%) by flattening on false-bear pullbacks. REFINEMENT 2026-08-21: regime_persist (EMA of breadth, span in bars) -> smoothed BIDIRECTIONAL deployment: ignores 1-bar pullbacks (protects good years) and goes to ~cash in a SUSTAINED bear (protects 2018/2022). || KEY 2026-08-21: regime_persist rd0.35+persist96 WON the sweep and was promoted (score -0.013 vs old champion -0.046). Validation 2018-2025: worst year -5.3% (2022), CAGR +41%. BUT the SEALED 2026 = -9.68% (old champion gave +0.4%). OVERFIT: 2021 +288% dominates the geometric CAGR; deployment fit the historical bulls and does NOT generalize to the sideways 2026. Cannot revert on 2026 (rule: 2026 is never feedback). LESSON: maximizing in-sample CAGR via deployment overfits; the criterion (worst+0.1cagr over 2018-2025) rewards configs that do not generalize. Needs ROBUSTNESS: walk-forward within 2018-2025, winsorize monster years, or meta-labeling. Methodology decision pending with rjj. || 2026-08-21: modular ensemble landed (orchestrator + 8 modules); meta-labeling built and A/B'd on validation -- a real drawdown-reducer (sealed 2026 -25%->-18% on a baseline config) but not a standalone fix; explored with regime + low exposure.

title: Decision modules improve OUT-OF-SAMPLE 2026 sharply
source: internal A/B (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-21)
summary: Same champion model; adding a light breadth risk-off (0.30) + a meta-label veto turns the SEALED 2026 readout from -23% to +16% and lifts the worst training year from -7.9% to -4.7%. Money-mgmt/martingale variants reach +19% in 2026 but clip the 2021 bull.
application: Confirms the modular stack earns its keep out-of-sample even when it costs a little in-sample CAGR. Motivates weighting robustness (worst-year / OOS) over raw CAGR in selection — the operator's open A11 decision. 2026 remains sealed and is never selected on.

title: Rolling one-year-hold reliability (invest any month, up in a year?)
source: operator criterion (2026-08-21) — the best algorithm is one where whenever you invest, a year later you're up
summary: Across 92 monthly cohorts 2018..2026 (incl. sealed 2026), each an independent account under the 25% mandate: the champion wins 75/92 (82%), median +23.3%, worst -16%. Adding decision modules LOWERS reliability (breadth/meta whipsaws -> 69/92, worst -25%). So the bare model is currently the most reliable on this lens.
application: Adopt the rolling 1-year win rate as a first-class evaluation criterion alongside the consistency law. New optimization target: raise 82% toward 100% without sacrificing median return. Now shown on every card as two headline numbers.

title: Global exposure-reduction levers LOWER rolling reliability
source: internal A/B (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-21)
summary: Both a breadth risk-off and volatility-targeting REDUCE the rolling one-year-hold win rate vs the bare champion (breadth 82->75%, vol 83->75% on research), because they clip the bull/recovery cohorts that make the win rate high, while only shallowly helping the bear-entry losers. The champion's ride-through is near-optimal among exposure levers.
application: Stop trying to raise rolling reliability with global exposure cuts. The lever must change ENTRY TIMING (a slower trend filter, A15) or act narrowly at capitulation, not size the whole book down.
result: breadth & vol both refuted for rolling

title: Champion is near-optimal for INCREMENTAL levers; raising rolling reliability needs an orthogonal move
source: internal A/B sweep (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-21)
summary: Three independent attempts to raise the 82% rolling one-year win rate all FAILED because each reduced bull/recovery participation: money-mgmt (clips bull), volatility-targeting (83->75%), and a longer 90d/120d trend filter (83->67% rolling, and terrible consistency). The winning cohorts come from catching the bull, so any global exposure/entry-timing cut loses more winners than it saves losers. The 17 losing cohorts are all shallow bear-entries.
application: Stop tweaking system-06 exposure/entry globally. To raise rolling reliability you need EITHER a narrow signal that acts ONLY at bear-entry/capitulation (A06 OHLCV proxy) OR a COMPLEMENTARY system (system 07) whose returns land exactly in system-06's losing periods (2018/2022 bears, 2026 dip) — diversification, not de-risking.

title: Raise reliability by DIVERSIFYING (a second system), not de-risking the first
source: internal R&D synthesis (system 06 loop, 2026-08-21)
summary: After 4 refutations (money, vol-target, longer-trend, standalone capitulation-add) all confirming that touching system 06 globally clips its bull-driven winning cohorts, the sound path to a higher rolling one-year win rate is a COMPLEMENTARY system whose returns land in system 06's losing periods (bear-entry cohorts of 2018/2022/2026). Capitulation dip-buying is the natural candidate — it earns in the sharp-drop/recovery regimes system 06 rides down.
application: Build system 07 as a separate long-only capitulation mean-reversion strategy using the tested capitulation feature; validate it has standalone positive-carry edge; then rolling-test a portfolio combine of 06+07 for a win rate above 82% without a median hit.

title: Capitulation dip-buying has a real, symbol-robust positive edge
source: internal edge study (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-21)
summary: Buying strong OHLCV capitulations (volume-spike + drop + lower-wick, score>0.4) and holding ~1-2 days returns +3% to +5% mean at 63-66% win net of 0.003 costs across BTC/ETH/SOL on 2018-2025 — vs +0.16% unconditional. The edge is real and strongest in the drop/bear regimes where the trend-following system 06 loses its bear-entry cohorts.
application: Build system 07 (a long-only capitulation dip-buyer) as a COMPLEMENT to system 06; a portfolio combine should lift the rolling one-year win rate above the champion's 82% because 07 earns exactly when 06 is weak. This is the operator's 'sum of systems' vision, now evidence-backed.

title: First ALL-POSITIVE champion, sealed 2026 also positive
source: autoloop iter 5 (2026-08-21)
summary: New system-06 champion: score +0.034 (first positive), EVERY year 2018-2025 up (worst +0.5%, 2022 now +4% vs prior -5%), CAGR +29.2%, and the SEALED 2026 readout is +3.3% (prior champion -9.7%). Config: min_hold 384 + breadth_gate 0.30 + regime_deploy 0.35. The breadth_gate 0.30 was seeded by the R&D loop (A01); combined with the longer-hold model it produced the all-positive result.
application: The 'profitable every year' badge is met on honest 2018-2025 selection, and it generalizes positively to the sealed forward year. This is the operator's core goal. Rolling reliability being recomputed to update the 82% baseline.

title: Capitulation dip-buying fails as a standalone system (falling knives)
source: internal backtest (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-21)
summary: A long-only capitulation dip-buyer, BTC and 14-symbol diversified, loses -11% to -24% and hits the 25% drawdown mandate on 2018-2025 research data. The per-event capitulation edge (+3-5%/trade, 65% win) does NOT survive sequential position management: capitulations cluster in cascades, so buying each one is catching falling knives in sustained bears. Diversification doesn't help because crashes are market-wide.
application: Dip-buying cannot safely earn in the sustained bears where the trend-follower system 06 is weak, so it is not a diversifying complement. Raising rolling reliability needs MODEL diversification (an ensemble of diverse champions) or is an operator criterion choice (A11), not a mean-reversion overlay.

title: Named-dict grid rows only pass whitelisted levers (fixed mom_gate/martingale)
source: internal (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-21)
summary: autoloop._row_to_kwargs keeps only keys in KNOWN_LEVERS (POSITIONAL ∪ MODULE_LEVERS). mom_gate and martingale were absent, so any grid row using them was silently reduced to its other levers — the lever was never tested. Added both to MODULE_LEVERS.
application: When seeding a module lever via a named-dict risk_grid row, ensure it is in MODULE_LEVERS or it is silently ignored. Fix applies on the next autoloop restart (Python doesn't hot-reload the running process).

title: Autoloop found a stronger all-positive champion (worst +5.2%, score +0.086)
source: autoloop iter 42 (2026-08-23)
summary: New system-06 champion: consistency +0.086 (prior +0.034), EVERY year 2018-2025 positive with WORST year +5.2% (prior +0.5%), CAGR +35%; sealed 2026 +0.4% (positive, lower than the prior +3.3% but 2026 is observation only). Config: 30d trend, min_hold 16 (short), breadth_gate 0.30 + regime 0.35. Found autonomously after ~37 iters.
application: Continuous autoloop improvement is real: the worst-year floor rose from +0.5% to +5.2% on honest 2018-2025 selection. Rolling reliability being recomputed to compare vs the retired 82%.

title: Raising calendar-year consistency LOWERS rolling one-year reliability
source: internal (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-23)
summary: Across three promoted champions the rolling one-year-hold win rate falls as the consistency score rises: 82% (worst -5%) -> 71% (worst +0.5%) -> 66% (worst +5.2%). Making every CALENDAR year positive (via short holds + a breadth risk-off) makes arbitrary-ENTRY-month 1-year holds LESS reliable and lowers median return vs the aggressive ride-through champion.
application: These are two different definitions of 'reliable' and they trade off. The autoloop selects on the consistency law, so it will keep drifting away from rolling reliability. The operator (A11) must choose which criterion selection should optimize — or a blend. 2026 stays sealed either way.

title: Generalized Hurst exponent (fractal market regimes)
source: Mandelbrot (1972); Di Matteo, Aste, Dacorogna (2003, generalized Hurst)
summary: H>0.5 = persistent/trending, H=0.5 = random walk, H<0.5 = anti-persistent/mean-reverting. The generalized Hurst from the q=1 structure function E[|dP(tau)|] ~ tau^H is a robust, causal, single-scalar regime measure.
application: New causal rolling-GHE channel; a Fractal module scales deployment by H so the book leans in only when the tape is genuinely persistent - bear-chop survival without a blanket exposure cut. Agenda A20.

title: Permutation entropy (ordinal complexity)
source: Bandt & Pompe, Phys. Rev. Lett. 88 (2002)
summary: Encodes a series by the ordinal patterns of consecutive values and takes the Shannon entropy of the pattern distribution - a fast, robust, model-free measure of how predictable vs random local dynamics are.
application: Gate entries when PE is high (noise) and upsize when low (legible). Agenda A21.

title: Log-periodic power law (bubble/crash prediction)
source: Sornette, Why Stock Markets Crash (2003); Johansen-Ledoit-Sornette model
summary: Bubbles grow faster-than-exponentially with accelerating log-periodic oscillations from herding/positive feedback; the LPPL fit estimates a critical time of change-of-regime.
application: Causal rolling LPPL confidence to de-risk before tops - protects near-top rolling cohorts. Agenda A22.

title: Topological early-warning (persistence landscapes)
source: Gidea & Katz, Physica A 491 (2018)
summary: The norm of the persistence landscape of a sliding window of returns rises sharply BEFORE major crashes (2000, 2008) - a topological signature of growing instability.
application: Cheap causal topological-stress scalar to de-risk on. Agenda A24.

title: Kalman local-level+slope adaptive trend
source: Kalman (1960); Harvey structural time-series models
summary: An optimal recursive state-space estimator of a latent level and slope; adapts its responsiveness to the signal-to-noise ratio, unlike a fixed-window moving average.
application: Replace/augment the fixed SMA trend gate to cut whipsaws at bear/bull transitions. Agenda A25.

title: Evolutionary optimization of the strategy genome
source: Holland (1975); evolutionary computation for rugged fitness landscapes
summary: Mutation+crossover+selection explores multimodal, non-differentiable search spaces more efficiently than uniform random sampling.
application: Evolve the config population on the consistency score instead of random search. Agenda A26.

title: Artificial immune system (negative selection)
source: Forrest et al. (1994); Aickelin danger theory
summary: Learn a model of self (normal) and flag non-self (anomalous) patterns - a biologically-inspired, model-agnostic novelty/anomaly detector.
application: De-risk when the live market bar is anomalous vs the learned normal regime. Agenda A27.

title: Behavioral sentiment extremes (fear & greed)
source: Kahneman-Tversky prospect theory; De Bondt-Thaler overreaction (1985)
summary: Crowds over-react at emotional extremes; a composite of vol, momentum, breadth and distance-from-high proxies the market emotional state for contrarian sizing.
application: Trim at greed peaks (protect rolling cohorts), press at fear lows. Agenda A28.
verdict: REFUTED (2026-08-24) as a contrarian sizer: on the iter-42 champion, feargreed=0.5 left the rolling one-year-hold win-rate unchanged (63/92=68% both) and COST upside (median +14.0%->+13.7%, best +524%->+455%) - trimming greed clipped the strongest cohorts. Worst cohort barely moved (-17%->-16%). No net rolling edge.

title: Cross-asset lead-lag / momentum cascade
source: Operator (2026-08-25); lead-lag & cross-sectional momentum literature (Lo/MacKinlay; crypto BTC-alt lead-lag studies)
summary: In a rally, assets fire sequentially (early movers -> BTC -> alt catch-up), not simultaneously. The state of the leaders/pack predicts the laggards - a causal cross-sectional edge distinct from simple breadth.
application: Horse-race channel: pack_heat + leader state + per-symbol laggard_gap -> upsize/enter laggards when the pack is firing. Agenda A30.

title: MM stop-hunt / liquidation-sweep detection
source: Operator (2026-08-25); market-microstructure stop-run / liquidity-grab patterns
summary: Market makers sweep two-sided stops (a candle with long upper AND lower wicks, high volume) then reverse; the sweep's geometry + volume + time-since-last-sweep is a causal, detectable pressure signal.
application: Two-sided sweep_score channel (extends capitulation.py); post-sweep contrarian reversal entries / pre-sweep vetoes. Agenda A31.

title: Decision tree over probabilistic + candlestick features
source: Operator; gradient boosting for tabular signals (Lopez de Prado feature engineering)
summary: A shallow tree/GBM over conditional-probability buckets and prior-bar candlestick shapes becomes a second directional voter alongside the oracle-NN, unblocking real multi-signal consensus.
application: Directional prob channel joined via consensus_k / weighted vote. Agenda A32 (unblocks A12).

title: Discipline diversity beats seed diversity
source: Operator; ensemble-of-experts / stacking; diversification of methods
summary: Combining models of DIFFERENT disciplines (trend, mean-reversion, cross-asset, microstructure) covers more regimes and is more robust than one model or seed-bagging alone - the route to profit in every year including out-of-sample 2026.
application: Formalise modules as directional voters and combine (vote/stack/consensus). Agenda A33.

title: Time-series foundation models (Chronos, TimesFM, Moment)
source: Ansari et al. 2024 (Chronos); Das et al. 2024 (TimesFM); Goswami et al. 2024 (Moment)
summary: Transformers pretrained on billions of diverse series produce strong zero-shot probabilistic forecasts - transfer learning for time series. More capable than anything trainable from scratch on one GPU.
application: Frozen local forecaster -> one causal forecast/uncertainty channel, A/B'd against our from-scratch nets. Agenda A36.

title: In low-signal finance, capacity is rarely the bottleneck
source: Israel, Kelly & Moskowitz 'Can Machines Learn Finance?' (2020); Lopez de Prado
summary: Financial panels have tiny signal-to-noise and non-stationarity; gains come from labels, regularization, data breadth and method diversity more than from bigger networks. Architecture upgrades must be A/B'd at equal budget, never assumed.
application: Guides A35/A36/A37 priority: data breadth first, pretrained knowledge second, architecture third. Agenda A35-A37.

title: The sealed-2026 flatness is an EDGE problem, not an exposure or sizing problem
source: internal analysis of the champion's per-year detail (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-25)
summary: The champion trades 87 times in sealed 2026 at 9.2% average exposure - comparable to 2022 (192 trades, 5.9%) and 2025 (175, 6.7%) - yet returns only +0.4%. It is NOT sitting in cash and it is NOT under-sized: its trades are simply break-even in that regime.
application: Therefore every SIZE-multiplier module (fear&greed, horse-race, sweep) is categorically incapable of fixing 2026: scaling a zero-edge trade by 1.3 leaves zero edge. Only a NEW SIGNAL with independent edge (A32 tree voter, A33 committee) or better generalization (bagging, purged validation) can change that year. This reframes the whole non-trend-alpha programme: prioritise DIRECTIONAL voters over sizing overlays.

title: TWO independent disciplines both invert in sealed 2026 - the problem is non-stationarity, not capacity
source: internal walk-forward edge measurement (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-25)
summary: The A32 decision tree (gradient boosting on candlestick shapes + probabilistic statistics) shows STRONG honest edge inside the research era: on 2.22M purged walk-forward verdicts, P(up)>0.55 bars return +0.338% over the next 32 bars vs -0.028% for P<0.45 (spread +0.365pp), with cleanly MONOTONIC deciles (-0.031 ... +0.438). On the sealed 2026 window the SAME model INVERTS: P>0.55 -> -0.139%, P<0.45 -> +0.034% (spread -0.174pp). The oracle-clone TCN fails the same way (break-even trades in 2026). Two completely different disciplines, different features, different labels, different inductive biases - both die in 2026.
application: This kills the 'bigger/better model' hypothesis: capacity is not the binding constraint, REGIME NON-STATIONARITY is. It also means any model selected purely on 2018-2025 can be anti-correlated in an unseen regime. The productive direction is regime-CONDITIONAL deployment (only vote where the regime resembles the one the edge was learned in - the Hurst/entropy channels exist for exactly this), plus genuine regime diversification, rather than more model classes trained the same way. Do NOT wire a raw voter that is known to be regime-fragile; make it regime-aware first, selected on research data only.

title: The tree edge is uniform across regimes AND years, then inverts in 2026 - regime-gating cannot fix it
source: internal research-only regime analysis (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-25)
summary: Bucketing 2.2M purged walk-forward verdicts by causal Hurst: the edge is POSITIVE in every bucket (H<0.45 +0.185pp, H 0.45-0.50 +0.381pp, H 0.50-0.55 +0.343pp, H>0.55 +0.445pp). Per calendar year it is positive EVERY year 2020-2025 (+0.264 to +0.515pp). In sealed 2026 it is negative in BOTH Hurst buckets (-0.082pp, -0.221pp).
application: A Hurst/fractal gate would NOT have prevented the 2026 failure, so the problem is not a regime our channels can see. An edge stable for six consecutive years that flips sign in the seventh is the signature of ALPHA DECAY / structural change (crowding, changed microstructure), not of a detectable regime. The productive responses are ADAPTIVITY (train on recent data so the model tracks the current market rather than the 2018-2025 average - testable on research alone by comparing rolling vs expanding windows on later years) and LIVE EDGE MONITORING (cut exposure when realized edge decays), not more model classes trained the same way on the same history.

title: Recency training is REFUTED: more history beats recent history, by a factor of three
source: internal 3-arm A/B, 16 quarterly purged folds (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-25)
summary: Three arms identical except the training window, judged on research years 2022-2025 only. Expanding (all resolved history, median 1.78M train rows) scored a +0.312pp edge spread; rolling 2y (775k rows) +0.110pp; rolling 1y (390k rows) +0.115pp. Rolling was worse in EVERY individual year (2022 .320 vs .196/.196; 2023 .283 vs .150/.074; 2024 .286 vs .213/.105; 2025 .402 vs .089/.157). As an observation only, no arm rescued the sealed window either (-0.176 expanding, -0.173 rolling-2y, -0.210 rolling-1y).
application: The intuitive fix for non-stationarity - 'retrain on recent data so the model tracks the current market' - is wrong here. The edge is faint and slow to estimate, so shrinking the sample costs far more in estimation variance than it gains in freshness, and no fitting scheme tracked the 2026 change. Combined with edge-inverts-not-regime-specific, this closes the door on both prediction (no regime signature) and adaptation (no refit tracks it). What remains is DETECTION AFTER THE FACT: monitor the realized expectancy of our own closed trades and cut exposure when it turns negative (A39). Corollary for the loop: prefer MORE data (A37 data breadth) over fresher data.

title: The champion could not be rebuilt from its own record: a 0.0 lever was dropped by truthiness
source: internal (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26) - caught while replicating the champion for the A37 universe test
summary: Replaying the iter-42 champion from best.json produced score -0.076 and worst year -11.3%, not the recorded +0.086 and +5.2%. The ledger sweep shows why: the winning row carried meta_margin 0.0, and both the ledger risk block and the model card recorded levers with `if brain_kwargs.get(lever)` - so 0.0, a perfectly active threshold, was silently skipped. The identical row WITHOUT the meta filter scores exactly what the replay produced (-0.0764, worst -11.2%), confirming the diagnosis.
application: Two consequences. (1) Reproducibility: anything rebuilding the champion from its record - the monitor card, the rolling-reliability job, an offline experiment, a future operator - was silently reconstructing a materially worse strategy. Fixed by recording levers by PRESENCE rather than truthiness, pinned by tests/test_lever_recording.py, and best.json/model_card.json were patched. (2) Substance: meta is not a marginal overlay, it is carrying the champion. Meta alone moves the score +0.163 (worst -11.2% -> +5.2%) on the same net, which is why every honest lever A/B keeps finding meta the star and the size-multiplier overlays marginal. Prefer levers of that kind - filters that refuse bad trades - over overlays that resize good ones.

title: A wider trading universe DILUTES a two-position book - breadth is not the lever
source: internal head-to-head, same net both arms (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: The champion net traded its own 14-symbol basket versus a 35-symbol superset (21 coins it never trained on), identical risk, per calendar year 2018-2025. Narrow scored -0.0760 with a -11.3% worst year and +36.7% CAGR; wide scored -0.1326 with a -15.4% worst year and +21.1% CAGR. Wide lost on every axis (score -0.057, worst -4.1pp, CAGR -15.6pp), with 2019 falling from +28% to -4% and 2024 from +14% to -8%.
application: With only two open positions, extra candidates do not diversify - they dilute. Every additional coin is another chance for a spurious high-conviction signal on a noisier, later-listed name to displace a good pick, and the ranking has no notion of symbol quality. So universe breadth is refuted as a lever AT THIS BOOK SIZE; revisit only alongside more positions or an explicit quality/liquidity prior. IMPORTANT: this does NOT test the other half of A37 - training on more symbols and TRADING the good 14 remains untested and is the honest way to ask whether more data helps the net (it needs a GPU retrain). The 35-symbol dataset is built and cached, so that experiment is cheap to run later.

title: The meta filter pays at zero margin; demanding a bigger expected edge is monotonically worse
source: internal grid sweep, same net all rows (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: On one net, against a breadth-0.30 baseline of -0.1647 (worst -18.0%): meta_margin 0.0 scored -0.0738 (worst -9.8%), 0.002 scored -0.1037 (worst -12.1%), 0.005 scored -0.1198 (worst -13.2%). A clean monotonic ordering - every step up in strictness costs score AND worst year. The meta filter itself is worth +0.091 of score here, echoing the +0.163 it is worth on the champion net.
application: The meta filter earns its keep by refusing trades whose expected net is NEGATIVE; raising the bar above zero starts refusing genuinely good trades, and the loss is immediate and monotonic. So keep meta_margin at 0.0 in the champion recipe and stop sweeping upward. More generally this sharpens the standing pattern - filters that refuse bad trades pay, multipliers that resize good trades do not - with an important boundary: a filter only pays while it is removing negative expectancy, not whenever it is made stricter.

title: Training on 2.5x the symbols does NOT make a better net - the data thesis is exhausted
source: internal A40 experiment (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: The champion genome was retrained on 35 symbols (4.95M windows, val accuracy 72.5%) and then traded ONLY the 14, with meta verdicts rebuilt and the champion's true risk config. It scored -0.1452 (worst -16.6%, CAGR +21.1%). The fair comparison is not the champion's +0.0864 (a max over many draws) but the recent fresh narrow-trained nets in the same config family, whose meta-0.0 rows have median -0.0815 and best -0.0359 - so the wide-trained net is still about 0.06 WORSE than a typical narrow-trained one. Caveat recorded honestly: the wide net auto-tuned to a different anti-churn band (min_hold 192 versus 16), which is part of the genome's realization rather than a bug.
application: Combined with A38 (fresher data is 3x worse than all history) and A37 (a wider TRADING universe dilutes a two-position book), the data thesis is now exhausted from all three directions: not fresher, not wider to trade, not wider to learn from. Stop buying data and start fixing SELECTION and FILTER quality.

title: The champion's score is close to what selection luck alone produces - and it has blocked the loop for 94 iterations
source: internal analysis of 136 completed iterations (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: Across 136 completed iterations the selected score has mean -0.0693 and standard deviation 0.0516; only 10 ever scored above zero. The champion's +0.0864 is the sample MAXIMUM - roughly three standard deviations above the mean and 2.5x the runner-up (+0.0342). The expected maximum of 136 draws from that distribution is about +0.057, so the champion's score is close to what selection luck alone yields. Meanwhile PROMOTE_MARGIN is 0.02, well BELOW the 0.052 selection noise, so the bar cannot distinguish a genuinely better strategy from a luckier one.
application: Two consequences, both large. (1) It explains the sealed-window collapse better than any market hypothesis: a champion that is mostly a lucky draw has no edge to carry forward, which is precisely what the 2026 readout shows. (2) It explains the operator's complaint that nothing has improved for days - the loop has been chasing a number that luck produced and has not promoted in 94 iterations. The fix is a ROBUST selection procedure: verify a candidate (and the incumbent) by re-running the same genome under different seeds and comparing a median rather than a single draw, and set the promotion margin relative to the measured selection noise instead of an arbitrary 0.02.

title: CONFIRMED: the champion's score is not reproducible - two reseeds land 0.20 below it
source: internal A41 reseed experiment (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: The champion's EXACT genome was retrained under seeds 43 and 44 and scored with its own risk config. Seed 43: -0.1054 (worst -12.0%, band min_hold 192). Seed 44: -0.1171 (worst -12.6%, min_hold 288). The champion as drawn: +0.0864 (worst +5.2%, min_hold 16). Median of the three draws: -0.1054. Both reseeds land about 0.20 below the champion and BELOW the 136-iteration population mean of -0.0693; even the auto-tuned anti-churn band failed to reproduce.
application: The champion was a lucky draw, and using its score as the promotion bar blocked every candidate for 94 iterations - the direct cause of the operator's complaint that nothing improves. Three changes followed: promotion is now seed-verified (a candidate that clears the bar on one draw is re-run under 2 more seeds and promoted only on the MEDIAN); PROMOTE_MARGIN was raised from 0.02 to 0.05, about one standard deviation of the measured selection noise, so the bar sits above the noise instead of below it; and the incumbent bar was reset to the genome's reproducible median (-0.1054), with the original record archived verbatim at champion_iter42_lucky_draw.json. The general rule now governing this system: a result that cannot be reproduced under a different seed is not a result.

title: A safety check that fails OPEN silently restores the bug it was built to remove
source: internal review of the seed-verification code before it first ran (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: The new promotion rule took the median of [candidate, verify_seed_1, verify_seed_2] and filtered out failures. But a failed verification is recorded as None, and filtering left a ONE-element list whose median is the candidate's own draw - so if verification ever errored (it is wrapped in try/except by design, to keep a failure from taking the loop down), promotion would quietly fall back to exactly the single-lucky-draw behaviour the rule exists to refuse. Nothing would have looked wrong in the logs.
application: The rule now FAILS CLOSED: any incomplete verification blocks the promotion, and the candidate simply gets another chance on a later iteration. A test pins it - a candidate that clears the bar on its own draw with failed verifications must not promote - and it was confirmed to fail against the filtering version. General lesson for this system: when a guard is wrapped in a try/except so it cannot crash the loop, check what happens to the DECISION when the guard fails, because the dangerous outcome is not a crash, it is a silent reversion.

title: A verification must measure the thing that ships, and measure it the same way as the bar
source: internal review during the first live verification (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: The first seed verification re-ran the candidate's genome by SEARCHING THE WHOLE RISK GRID, so each verification received its own best-of-ten selection. The incumbent bar, by contrast, was measured as the reproducible median of ONE configuration (the champion genome plus its winning risk config). Candidates were therefore being measured more generously than the bar they had to clear - a max-of-ten against a single configuration - which biases toward promotion and quietly reintroduces the selection advantage the guard exists to remove.
application: Verification now scores the WINNING configuration only: the exact pair of genome and risk settings that would ship. That makes the candidate and the incumbent commensurable, strips the best-of-grid advantage out of the check, and costs roughly a tenth of the backtests (eight instead of eighty), which matters because each verification pass is a full pipeline. Two tests pin it - one asserting the grid search is never called and that zero-valued levers such as meta_margin 0.0 reach the backtest, another asserting a failed verification returns None so the fail-closed rule can refuse. General lesson: when adding a check, ask not only whether it can fail, but whether it measures the same quantity as the threshold it is compared against.

title: First seed-verified champion: positive in all nine years, including the sealed window
source: autoloop promotion under the new verified rule (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: A candidate drew +0.0675 (worst +3.8%, CAGR +29.2%, all-positive 2018-2025). Rather than crowning it, the loop re-ran the genome under two fresh seeds: -0.1137 and -0.0132. The median of the evidence cleared the reset bar, so it promoted. Its per-year record is positive in EVERY year: 2018 +20.5, 2019 +8.9, 2020 +14.3, 2021 +281, 2022 +5.9, 2023 +8.4, 2024 +14.0, 2025 +3.8, and the SEALED 2026 readout is +4.2% at 10.0% drawdown on 64 trades - against the previous champion's +0.4%. Genome: threshold 0.03, window 96, 50 epochs, lr 1e-3, dropout 0.1, trend_span 5760 (60d), uniqueness weighting ON; band 0.75/0.25/16; risk breadth 0.30, regime 0.35, meta_margin 0.005.
application: The first champion this system has promoted on reproducible evidence rather than a single draw. Two honest caveats travel with it. Its own re-runs scored far below its headline, so the SHIPPED weights remain a favourable draw of a genome whose reproducible level is much lower - which is exactly why the bar for future candidates is now its verification median, not its headline. And the 2026 number is an observation, never a selection input; it is encouraging precisely because nothing was optimised against it, but one window is not proof.

title: CORRECTION: the best meta margin is net-dependent, not universally zero
source: internal grid observation across two nets (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: On the first net the ordering was clean and monotonic - baseline -0.1647, meta 0.0 -0.0738, 0.002 -0.1037, 0.005 -0.1198 - which suggested zero was optimal and stricter thresholds only refused good trades. The very next promoted champion won with meta_margin 0.005. The earlier reading was true of that net, not of the system.
application: Supersedes meta-margin-zero-is-optimal as a general claim: the meta threshold interacts with the net, so the sweep must stay in the grid rather than being collapsed to a single value. This is also a caution about acting on n=1 monotonicity - the ordering was clean and still did not generalise. The plan to prune the 0.002 and 0.005 rows for throughput is cancelled; the cheaper throughput win came from making verification score one configuration instead of searching the grid.

title: Every genome tested so far reproduces near -0.10, whatever its headline draw
source: five independent reseeds across two champion genomes (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: Old champion (headline +0.0864): reseeds -0.1054 and -0.1171. New champion (headline +0.0675, all-positive 2018-2025): loop verifications -0.1137 and -0.0132, and a fixed-config reseed at -0.0993 with a worst year of -12.2%. Five re-runs of two different genomes, and with one exception they land between -0.10 and -0.12 - well below both headlines and below the -0.0693 mean of the per-iteration selected scores. Even the auto-tuned anti-churn band fails to reproduce: the same genome has chosen min_hold 16, 96, 192 and 288 across draws.
application: The honest reading is uncomfortable and worth stating plainly: this system has not yet found a genome that RELIABLY produces an all-positive record. It has found draws that did. The reproducible level of the current search space - this TCN family over this risk grid - sits near -0.10, meaning a worst calendar year around minus twelve percent, and the all-positive champions are favourable draws sitting on top of that. Two consequences follow. First, celebrating a headline is not progress; only moving the reproducible level is. Second, the most direct attack on the problem is to reduce the seed variance itself rather than to keep drawing from it - which is exactly what bagged ensembles do, and search.json already samples ensemble sizes 1 and 3. The clean next experiment is to reseed an ensemble-of-3 genome and ask whether the gap between its headline and its re-runs is smaller than for a single net.

title: Rolling one-year-hold reliability reaches 85%, the best this system has recorded
source: internal rolling_12m on the promoted champion's true config (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: On the operator's own criterion - invest in any month, be up a year later - the new champion wins 78 of 92 monthly cohorts (85%), against 63 of 92 (68%) for the champion it replaced and 75 of 92 (82%) for the best previously recorded. Worst cohort -18% (versus -17%), median +10.2% (versus +14.0%), best +380% (versus +524%). Computed on its TRUE config, meta filter attached, over combined data including the sealed window as an observation.
application: The trade is explicit and is the one the operator asked for: less upside concentration in exchange for far more consistency. Fifteen more monthly cohorts finish the year in profit, while the median cohort gives up about four points and the luckiest gives up a lot. Worth stating alongside the caveat that the promoted weights remain a favourable draw - but note this is measured on the SHIPPED artifact, so it is what the operator would actually have experienced.

title: The reproducible level moved for the first time: -0.1054 to -0.0885
source: like-for-like fixed-config reseeds of both champions (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: The old champion's shipping configuration reseeded to -0.1054 and -0.1171 (median -0.1054). The new champion's reseeded to -0.0993 and -0.0776 (median -0.0885), with worst years of -12.2% and -8.4%. Same method both times, so the comparison is like for like.
application: This is the first genuine progress by the only measure that counts under the governing rule: not a better headline, but a better level that survives re-seeding. The improvement is modest (+0.017) and the level is still negative, meaning the reproducible worst year remains around minus nine to twelve percent - so the goal of reliable annual profit is not met. But the bar now moves on evidence rather than luck, and the promotion machinery updated it automatically, which is exactly what it was built to do.

title: Three separate places set the promotion bar, and two of them undid the fix
source: internal audit after a qualifying candidate failed to trigger verification (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: An iteration scored -0.0128 against a reproducible bar of -0.0885 - comfortably qualifying - yet its ledger row carried no verify_scores, so verification never ran. The cause was that the bar was set in three places and only one of them had been corrected. The loop initialised it by reading best.json's headline score directly (+0.0675) instead of through _read_best_score, which prefers the reproducible median; the per-iteration refresh only ever RAISED the bar, so a corrected lower value on disk could never take effect; and a promotion reset it to the winning draw rather than to that champion's reproducible median.
application: Net effect: candidates needed to beat +0.1175, so verification would essentially never fire and the search was silently back in the stall the whole regime was built to end - with every individual piece looking correct in isolation. All three now flow from _read_best_score, the disk is authoritative in BOTH directions so a corrected bar can lower as well as raise, and promotion stores the reproducible median. A test pins the end-to-end behaviour with the real numbers. General lesson: when a quantity governs a decision, it needs ONE source; a fix applied to the reader is worthless while other writers still set it the old way.

title: Measured: choosing the best of ten risk configs inflates the reported score by 0.077
source: internal analysis of 125 full grid sweeps in the ledger (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: For every iteration the loop reports the MAX over its risk grid. Across 125 sweeps that max averages -0.0608 while the MEDIAN configuration on the very same net averages -0.1373. The gap - the inflation contributed purely by picking the best of ten on the same eight years that score them - averages +0.0765 (median +0.0720, stdev 0.0431, quartiles 0.040 and 0.103). For scale: reseeding a FIXED configuration moves the score by only about 0.01 to 0.02, while the champion's headline-to-reseed gap was about 0.15.
application: This decomposes the lucky-champion phenomenon numerically. Of the ~0.15 gap between a champion's headline and what it reproduces, roughly half is grid selection (0.077) and the rest is which net happened to be drawn; the seed applied to a FIXED configuration contributes almost nothing. Three consequences. First, it VALIDATES the current design: verification reseeds a fixed configuration, which is exactly the estimate that carries no selection inflation, which is why the reproducible bar sits about 0.077 below the headlines. Second, it PREDICTS that bagging will not solve this - ensembles reduce seed variance, the smallest term, so A43 should not produce a large improvement (its first ensemble scored -0.1288, consistent with that). Third, the remaining honest improvement is to stop selecting and scoring the risk configuration on the same years - a nested or held-out selection - or simply to treat the median of the grid, not its max, as the iteration's real result.

title: The guard refused its first promotion: a qualifying draw that did not reproduce
source: autoloop verification, first refusal (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: A candidate drew -0.0382, clearing the bar of -0.0885 plus a 0.05 margin by less than a thousandth. Its two fixed-config reseeds returned -0.1447 and -0.1120, so the median sat far below the threshold and the loop printed 'NOT promoted: single draw -0.0382 did not survive re-seeding'. The whole check resolved in about an hour, against roughly two and a half before verification was changed to score the shipping configuration instead of re-searching the grid.
application: Under the old rule this draw would have become the champion, and its per-year record - worst year -5.8%, CAGR +20.1% - would have looked respectable enough to set a bar that later candidates could not clear. Instead it was measured and rejected in an hour. Note also that the gap between the draw and its reseeds, about 0.09, matches the independently measured grid-selection inflation of 0.077 plus draw luck - the decomposition predicting the individual case correctly is decent evidence it is right.

title: Background GPU experiments collide with the autoloop and die mid-run
source: A43 seed 245 crash (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: The third ensemble seed trained successfully (val accuracy 66.5%) and then died during signal export with 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered', because the experiment and the autoloop were both using the single GPU. The autoloop was unharmed; the background job lost roughly ninety minutes of completed training - or would have, had the model not been written to disk first.
application: Two operational rules follow. Run background experiments on CPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1) whenever they only need inference or backtesting, which is most of them - export, meta and scoring are all CPU-viable and merely slower. When a job genuinely needs the GPU to train, expect collisions and structure it so the expensive artifact is SAVED before anything else happens, so a crash costs minutes rather than hours. That structure is what allowed seed 245 to be recovered by redoing only the export and scoring, on CPU, instead of retraining.

title: REFUTED: bagging made the result FIVE TIMES less reproducible, not more
source: A43, three ensemble seeds against two single-net seeds of the same genome (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: Same genome, same risk configuration, fixed-config scoring throughout. Ensemble of three nets: -0.1288, -0.1845, -0.0718 (spread 0.1127, mean -0.1283). Single net: -0.0776, -0.0993 (spread 0.0217, mean -0.0885). So averaging three seed-varied networks produced a spread five times WIDER and a mean about 0.04 WORSE, at three times the training cost.
application: The intuition was that averaging seeds removes seed variance, and it was wrong in the only way that matters - end to end. The mechanism visible in the data: bagging pulls the averaged probabilities toward the middle, so the fraction of bars above 0.5 fell from about 50.5% for single nets to 45.8% and 47.6% for ensembles. The anti-churn band optimiser then compensates, and it chose wildly different bands across the three runs (min_hold 288, 96, 288, with different enter and exit levels). Variance did not disappear; it MOVED from the network into the band selection, and amplified on the way. Two lessons. Reducing variance in a component does not reduce it in the system if a downstream selector is free to react. And this is the second time a nested max-selection has been the culprit: the band optimiser picks the best band on validation exactly as the risk grid picks the best configuration on the research years, so BOTH are multiple-comparisons steps that inflate and destabilise.

title: The system contains TWO nested best-of selections, and both inflate
source: synthesis of the grid-inflation measurement and the ensemble refutation (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: Each iteration performs two maximisations before reporting a number. The training step sweeps the anti-churn band and keeps the best on validation. The risk step sweeps ten configurations and keeps the best across the research years - measured at +0.077 of inflation. The ensemble experiment showed the band step is not benign either: with smoothed probabilities it chose min_hold 288, 96 and 288 across three runs of the same genome, and the resulting scores spread five times wider than single nets.
application: Every reported score is a max of a max, so it is optimistic twice over, and the instability of one selector can be hidden or amplified by the other. This reframes what to fix: not the model, the data or the ensemble, but the two selection steps. Concretely - hold out years for the risk selection rather than choosing and scoring on the same ones, and either fix the band or select it on data that does not also score it. It also explains why verification had to score ONE configuration to be honest: that is the only measurement in the system with no maximisation inside it.

title: OPERATOR MANDATE (2026-08-26): consistency is achieved-ish, now MAXIMISE profit
source: operator message, 2026-08-26
summary: The operator reviewed the new champion (all years positive, 85% rolling reliability, sealed 2026 +4.2%) and accepts the integrity and capital preservation, but says 4% in a full year is far too little. One caveat they raised themselves: one specific year always comes out well because everything rises in it, so winning it carries little merit compared with winning bear years. The new order of priorities: keep the guarantees (small drawdowns, capital preservation, every-year-positive) but MAXIMISE profit in bull, bear and sideways markets alike.
application: Two routes named by the operator: raise the hit rate, or work specifically on MONEY MANAGEMENT - and for the latter they explicitly proposed replacing rule-based money management with a LEARNED MODEL (see A45). Scoring consequence: the consistency law (worst year + 0.10*CAGR) already encodes 'positive every year', but its CAGR weight of 0.10 is small; once candidates reliably clear all_positive, the CAGR term is the one to grow. Do NOT change the law mid-experiment on this message alone - first find candidates that clear the bar reproducibly, then revisit the weight.

title: REFUTED: tranche entries and trailing partial exits lose on every variant at 15m
source: A46 fast-sim screen, champion signals + shipping config, research years 2018-2025 (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: Six variants against the baseline, both arms in the same simulator, baseline pinned to the production fast sim (drift 0.00000, 1073/1073 trades on the sanity year). Baseline: score -0.0839, worst year -10.3%, mean +19.3%, 9136 trades, exposure 9.1%. Two tranches: score -0.1023, mean collapses to +8.7%, trades +64%. Three tranches: mean +3.8%, trades +97%. Trailing half-exit at trail_stop/2: score -0.1109 and the WORST year gets worse (-12.6%), because it sells winners into ordinary pullbacks and locks losses in downtrends while the remainder still rides to the full trail. Combinations lose too. Every variant is worse on the consistency score.
application: The kill criterion fired exactly as written: at 15-minute bars with a 0.30% round-trip toll, the extra band crossings eat the benefit - churn control (min_hold hysteresis) exists precisely because fees dominate at this granularity, and tranching multiplies crossings. Tranching also CUTS exposure (9.1% to 5.6-7.0%), and exposure scarcity is already this system's binding profit constraint - so progressive entries attack the problem from the wrong side. Two things survive the refutation: (1) do not touch the shared backtester for fractional positions - the screen killed the justification before any engine risk was taken; (2) partial exits might still earn a place LATER via A45, if a learned sizing model finds specific states where trimming has positive expectancy - but as a blanket mechanical rule it is refuted. Caveat recorded honestly: screened without breadth/regime/meta overlays (they only shrink exposure further, which strengthens the conclusion), adds were confirmation-only (into strength, 2h spacing); averaging-down variants were not tested here because bounded martingale was already tested separately in-loop.

title: Per-trade expectancy concentrates in observable entry states, in EVERY year
source: A45 stage 1 trade-opportunity map: 22,439 champion-rule entries, research years (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: Mapping every entry the champion's rule would take (per symbol, champion exits) gives 22,439 trades: mean +0.17% net, median -0.45%, win 43% - a thin, skewed edge. But expectancy is strongly state-dependent: top-vs-bottom quartile spreads are +0.83pp for entry volatility, +0.70pp for momentum, +0.58pp for model probability, +0.44pp for trend age - each 3-4x the average trade's whole expectancy. Hurst is FLAT (consistent with the refuted hurst gate). Per-year check: the vol gradient is positive in 8 of 8 years, momentum 8 of 8, prob 7 of 8 - this is NOT 2021 in disguise, though 2021 carries most of the raw profit (+34.45 of +38.44 summed net). Stops are the concentrated drag: 567 trades at -9.7% each.
application: This is the evidence A45 needed: sizing has something to learn. The features are all per-bar computable and already exported as channels, so a learned sizing model can be wired exactly like the tree channel (walk-forward npz + off-by-default module).

title: Walk-forward learned sizing lifts expectancy ~45% relative, and never materially hurts
source: A45 stage 2: HistGradientBoosting on the trade map, expanding walk-forward with 1-month embargo, OOS 2019-2025 (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: Train on all trades strictly before the test year (December of the prior year embargoed), predict per-trade net (clipped +/-20% so 2021 moonshots cannot dominate), map TRAIN-quintile boundaries to size multipliers 0.5/0.75/1.0/1.5/2.0, score capital-normalised expectancy. Sized beats flat in 5 of 7 OOS years; mean lift +0.08pp per trade on a +0.17pp base (~+45% relative); worst year costs -0.0001 (2019). In the 2022 bear it REDUCES losses (+0.09pp). OOS rank spread Q4-Q1 positive in 5 of 7 years, up to +1.5pp (2021) and +0.79pp (2024).
application: The profile is exactly what a size-multiplier module wants: meaningful average gain, no material harm in any year, loss-reducing in the bear. Caveat recorded: this is TRADE-level; the portfolio takes only 2 concurrent positions through breadth/regime/meta filters, so the portfolio-level effect must be established by the loop's own risk-grid A/B before any belief is updated. Next: export a per-bar sizing channel exactly like tree.npz (expanding annual retrain for research years, research-only final model for the sealed window), a SizingModel module mapping the channel to size_mult via stored train-quintile bounds, tests, then a money_model row in risk_grid.json so the autoloop judges it on the real engine per-year.

title: PREDICTION (recorded before the A/B): the learned sizing model is PRO-CYCLICAL
source: direct inspection of moneymodel.npz at champion entry states (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: At the 261,502 bars where the champion's entry rule actually fires, the learned multiplier averages 1.073 - mildly expansionary overall - but the year pattern is systematic: 2021 (the big bull) 1.253, 2020 1.112, 2024 1.114, against 2022 (bear) 0.979, 2025 0.976 and the sealed 2026 window 0.902. The model sizes UP in rising markets and DOWN in flat or falling ones. Note the distribution over ALL bars (49.7% at the 0.5x floor) is not the relevant statistic - most bars are not entry states - which is why the entry-conditioned mean is the number that matters.
application: This makes a falsifiable prediction, recorded BEFORE the loop's A/B returns: the money_model row should IMPROVE the consistency score (it cuts size in the bad years, matching the walk-forward finding that it reduces 2022 losses) while REDUCING profit in flat years - including the sealed window, where it would cut an already-minimal 0.8% average exposure by a further tenth. If that is what the per-year sweep shows, then learned sizing is a risk-management win and a profit LOSS, which is the opposite of the operator's stated priority, and the honest response is to invert the mapping's asymmetry (raise the cap, lift the floor) rather than to celebrate the score. The 2026 figure here is an observation only and enters no decision; the verdict comes from the research years.

title: Measured: the band sweep inflates by +0.081, and its winner wins ZERO individual years
source: champion risk config scored under all 72 bands per research year, fast sim (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: Scoring the champion's shipping risk configuration under every band in train.py's grid (4 enters x 3 exits x 6 holds): max -0.0183, median -0.0994, so choosing the best of 72 on the same eight years that score them inflates by +0.0811 - essentially the same magnitude as the risk grid's +0.0765. Spread across bands is large (min -0.2416, stdev 0.0430). The decisive number is the stability check: the overall winning band (enter 0.75, exit 0.35, min_hold 288) wins ZERO of the eight years individually, and no band wins more than one. The champion's own band (0.75/0.25/16) ranks 24th of 72.
application: Two selections, +0.0765 and +0.0811, sum to about 0.158 - which matches almost exactly the ~0.15 gap repeatedly observed between a champion's headline and what its genome reproduces. The decomposition is now complete and quantitative: nearly the whole gap is selection optimism, not model quality. And a band that wins the aggregate while winning no individual year is a multiple-comparisons artefact by definition, so the sweep is not finding a setting - it is finding noise. This justifies pinning the band as a searched genome dimension (mechanism already shipped) rather than letting train() maximise over it. Corollary for the fast-sim caveat: this measurement omits breadth/regime/meta overlays, but those shrink exposure uniformly across bands and cannot manufacture a spread of this size.

title: THE RECURRING BUG CLASS: the bar and the candidate must measure the same quantity
source: caught before shipping, third occurrence (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-26)
summary: This system has now produced the same bug three times in different clothes. (1) The bar was a lucky max-of-grid headline while candidates were compared against it - a stall of 94 iterations. (2) Verification re-searched the risk grid, giving each re-run its own best-of-ten while the bar was a fixed-config median. (3) Now: the bar on disk (-0.0885) came from verification re-runs that each swept the whole 72-band grid, so it CARRIES band inflation; the moment search.json pins bands, candidates would be measured about 0.08 lower than the incumbent and nothing could ever be promoted again - the exact mirror of (1).
application: The general rule, worth stating once and applying forever: whenever a maximisation is REMOVED from the candidate's measurement, the incumbent bar must be re-measured without it in the same breath, and whenever one is ADDED the same. A bar is not a number, it is a MEASUREMENT PROCEDURE, and comparing two different procedures is meaningless however careful the arithmetic. Practically, that means any change to _score_genome's measurement path requires re-running the incumbent through the new path before the change goes live. Caught this time before it ran, by asking what the bar on disk was actually measured with rather than assuming.

title: Learned sizing, first two portfolio A/Bs: neutral then clearly positive - and my prediction was WRONG
source: loop ledger iterations 1-2 under seed 48913, config 7 vs config 11 on the same net (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Clean same-net comparison, incumbent (meta_margin 0.005) against the identical row plus money_model 1.0. Iteration 1: score -0.0011, worst year unchanged, CAGR -0.0114 - a wash, with large offsetting per-year moves (2019 -21.6pp, 2021 -39.8pp against 2020 +20.7pp, 2024 +19.9pp, 2025 +11.9pp). Iteration 2: score +0.0206, worst year +0.0147 (from -5.9% to -4.5%), CAGR +0.0587, driven by 2021 +61.6pp and 2025 +10.1pp, with the 2022 bear also improving +1.5pp - and the money_model row WON the whole eleven-row grid, becoming that iteration's reported score.
application: The prediction recorded before these results - that pro-cyclical sizing would raise the consistency score while REDUCING profit in flat years - is not supported, and the reasoning behind it was wrong in an instructive way. I reasoned from the mean multiplier per year at entry states (1.25 in the 2021 bull, 0.98 in the 2022 bear), but the portfolio outcome is dominated by WHICH trades get upsized, not by the average multiplier: amplifying the right trades in 2021 added 61.6 points while the average multiplier was only 1.25, and the bear year improved rather than deteriorated. Lesson worth keeping: an average over entry states does not predict a portfolio outcome when the book holds only two positions at a time and selection interacts with sizing.
