Verdict so far: two samples, one neutral and one clearly positive, is encouraging and NOT conclusive - keep the row in the grid and accumulate. Caveat to state plainly: the overlay is built from the CHAMPION's signals while these iterations score different nets, so the sizing features come from one net and the trades from another; that mismatch can only understate what a per-net overlay would do, which makes the positive sample more interesting rather than less.

title: The debiased trigger did its job on its second live iteration
source: loop ledger iteration 2 under seed 48913 (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Iteration 2 reported -0.0157, which clears the -0.0885 bar by seven hundredths and would have triggered a verification (~2 GPU-hours) under the old rule. Debiased by the measured grid inflation it sits at -0.0922 and does NOT clear, so no seeds were spent. Its own grid_inflation was +0.143. Running per-iteration inflation values: +0.0875, +0.0931, +0.048, +0.143 - median about +0.09, noisier per iteration than the +0.0765 aggregate but of the same size.
application: This is the fix behaving exactly as designed on live data rather than in a backtest of the ledger: the trigger refused to spend verification compute on a score whose apparent margin was entirely selection optimism. It also shows the inflation is heteroscedastic - it varies a lot per iteration - which argues for keeping the ledger-median prior (already implemented, activating once eight rows carry the field) rather than the frozen constant.

title: BREAKTHROUGH: the band sweep optimised the WRONG objective and cost ~0.10 of score
source: controlled A/B on identical seeds, pinned vs swept (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Same genome, same risk config, same seeds, only the band handling differs. Seed 91001: swept -0.1666 against pinned +0.0057. Seed 91002: swept -0.0329 against pinned +0.0000. Swept median -0.0997 - which lands on the old band-swept bar of -0.0885, confirming that bar was representative rather than unlucky - against a pinned median of +0.0029. Sweeping the band costs about 0.10 of consistency score. The mechanism is visible in the run log: train() chooses the band that maximises PER-SYMBOL VALIDATION NET-OF-TOLL RETURN, and for seed 91002 it picked enter 0.85 / exit 0.15 / min_hold 288 with 97 trades per symbol and +143% validation net return - four times the pinned band's +33% - yet that band scored WORSE on the law that actually judges the genome (worst calendar year + 0.10*CAGR on a two-position portfolio).
application: The general lesson is bigger than the band: HARD MAXIMISATION ON A MISALIGNED PROXY IS WORSE THAN NO MAXIMISATION AT ALL. Optimising a proxy does not merely fail to help, it actively selects the configurations where proxy and true objective diverge most - the harder you optimise, the further you travel from the goal. That also explains two standing puzzles: why the champion's own band ranks only 24th of 72 on the consistency score, and where A43's missing variance went. Pinned re-runs are about 20x more reproducible than swept ones (spread 0.006 vs 0.134), so the band optimiser was the variance source all along; bagging failed because it pushed MORE variance into that optimiser instead of removing it. Shipped: the band is now an explicit searched gene (band_enter/band_exit/band_hold), pinned identically in the search and verification paths, subject to the same seed-verified promotion as every other lever. Standing check for any future proxy: before optimising something, confirm it is measuring what the final score measures.

title: The reproducible level crossed from -0.10 to roughly ZERO
source: band-pinned re-measurement of the champion genome (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: The reproducible bar has moved -0.1054 (August 26, old champion) -> -0.0885 (new champion) -> +0.0029 (same champion, band pinned). Under the governing rule - a result that cannot be reproduced under a different seed is not a result - this is the first time the level has reached break-even. Two seeds, and unusually trustworthy ones: pinned re-runs cluster within 0.006, against 0.134 for swept.
application: Score = worst calendar year + 0.10*CAGR, so a level near zero means the reproducible WORST YEAR is now close to break-even rather than the -10% to -12% that had persisted through every previous measurement. That is the operator's consistency requirement approached honestly rather than by a lucky draw, and it came from removing a bad optimisation rather than from adding model capacity - after data, breadth, recency, ensembles and every sizing overlay had each been refuted. Caveats to keep attached: two seeds is thin evidence however tight; the number describes the CHAMPION's genome with its own band, and other genomes must earn their own; and the profit mandate is untouched by this - a break-even worst year is capital preservation, not yet the profit the operator asked for. That is what A45 is for.

title: FOURTH instance of the bug class: a correction must be estimated in the regime it corrects
source: caught by inspection while verifying the band-pinning rollout (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: The debiased trigger subtracts a grid-inflation prior estimated as the median of ledger rows carrying `grid_inflation`. That reader pooled EVERY row - so once eight existed it would have blended band-swept iterations with band-pinned ones. The two regimes do not measure the same thing: pinning shifted the score level by about 0.10 and cut run-to-run spread roughly twentyfold. With five swept rows already on file, the very next three pinned iterations would have produced a contaminated median, and pinned candidates would have been debiased by a number partly derived from swept runs.
application: Same family as bar-must-measure-what-candidates-measure, now seen four times, and worth generalising beyond bars: ANY quantity used to adjust a comparison - a bar, a correction, a prior, a baseline - must be estimated from data produced the same way as the thing it adjusts. Fixed by filtering rows to the current regime (all three band genes present or absent) and requiring the minimum count within that regime, falling back to the constant otherwise. The fallback is itself regime-mismatched, since the constant was measured under sweeping - stated in the docstring rather than hidden, and tolerable only because it is a stand-in that expires once pinned rows accumulate. Tests pin both directions: a pinned loop must NOT borrow plentiful swept rows, and a swept loop must not borrow pinned ones.

title: CORRECTION: pinning beats sweeping only for a GOOD band, not for any band
source: first pinned iteration + declared sub-grid measurement (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: I predicted that reported scores would rise by about 0.10 once the band was pinned. The first pinned iteration scored -0.0922, BELOW the band-swept historical mean of -0.0674. One sample proves little against a distribution with a spread of 0.05 or more, but examining why exposed a real flaw in the prediction rather than in the change. The controlled experiment measured the CHAMPION's genome pinned to the CHAMPION's band against sweeping, and found +0.10. The search, however, now draws bands from a sixteen-combo space, and an arbitrary band is not the champion's. Measuring that declared sub-grid on the champion's risk config gives a median of -0.0934 against a full-grid median of -0.0994 and a swept result of -0.0997 - so SWEEPING BUYS ABOUT WHAT A RANDOM BAND BUYS, and the gain came from pinning a good band, not from pinning as such.
application: The A44 result stands but must be stated correctly: the band sweep does not FIND a good band, it lands near the median of the grid while spending a 72-way maximisation to get there, and a good band is worth roughly 0.10 over that. So the value of pinning is that the band becomes a searchable, verifiable gene - subject to seed-verified promotion like every other lever - not that any pinned band is better. It follows that early pinned iterations will look mediocre while the search samples bands, and that the gene pool matters enormously: the champion's known-good band must be available to breed from. Caveat on the sub-grid numbers themselves: they come from the fast simulator, which ranked the champion's band 7th of 16 while the real per-year simulator makes it the best point measured (+0.0029 against -0.0997) - so fast-sim band RANKINGS do not transfer, and only the spread (about 0.19 across the sub-grid) should be read from them.

title: FIFTH instance: the elite gene pool ranked across incomparable regimes
source: found while investigating the failed prediction (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: The evolutionary sampler breeds from the ledger's best-scoring genomes. That ranking pooled band-swept and band-pinned rows, which are not comparable - and since sweeping lands near the band-grid median while a random pinned band can land anywhere in a 0.19 spread, swept rows would have kept every elite slot. No pinned genome could ever have become a parent, so the band gene would have been sampled at random forever and evolution would never have converged on it.
application: The same bug family as the bar, the correction and the prior - five instances now - and the same cure: rank within the current regime, falling back to all rows only while too few exist, which is safe because a projected genome contributes genes and never a score. Added alongside it: the incumbent champion is now ALWAYS a breeding parent, folded back into genome form from its recorded band, since after a regime change the ledger may hold no row of the new regime good enough to seed the search. The incumbent is refused rather than half-used if it cannot fill the space or carries a value outside it, because a partial parent would be completed with random genes and would not be the champion at all.

title: The sizing channel is now rebuilt per net, removing the handicap it carried
source: A45 stage 4 (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: The first learned-sizing channel was built once from the CHAMPION's signals, so every candidate genome was sized by a model trained on a DIFFERENT net's trades - a handicap that could only understate the lever, and one that made the A/B evidence (positive in three of four samples) more interesting rather than less. It now rebuilds from each iteration's own signals, exactly as the meta-label channel already did, with the exit rules taken from the money_model grid row itself so the model learns the outcomes of the very rules it will size. Measured cost with the loop's already-loaded bars: 22.7 seconds against a roughly ninety-minute iteration, about four tenths of one percent.
application: Two design points worth keeping. First, the precedent mattered more than the invention: meta was already rebuilt per iteration for exactly this reason ('so the verdicts never drift from the signals they judge'), and following that pattern rather than improvising kept the walk-forward discipline intact. Second, the VERIFICATION path rebuilds it too and FAILS CLOSED - if a config calls for sizing and the channel cannot be built, the verification returns None and blocks promotion rather than quietly scoring a strategy without sizing against a bar that includes it. That would have been the sixth instance of this system's recurring measurement-mismatch bug, and it was designed out rather than discovered later.

title: PATTERN, now three times: variance moves to whichever selector is still free
source: pinned vs swept grid inflation, plus the A43 and band-pinning results (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Third independent sighting of one behaviour. (1) A43: stabilising the NETWORK with bagged ensembles did not stabilise the result - the anti-churn band optimiser compensated for the smoothed probabilities and the spread grew five times WIDER. (2) Band pinning: removing the band maximisation cut run-to-run spread about twentyfold (0.134 to 0.006), confirming the band optimiser had been holding that variance. (3) Now, with the band fixed, the RISK GRID's measured inflation rose from a swept-era median of +0.0875 to a pinned median of +0.1142 - the variance the band was absorbing has reappeared in the remaining selector.
application: Treat a chain of selectors as a system with a roughly conserved quantity of exploitable noise: constraining one does not destroy that noise, it relocates it to whichever step is still free to react. Two practical consequences. First, any correction estimated for one selector must be RE-measured after another is constrained - the swept-era 0.0765 now under-corrects by about 0.038, which is why the prior is regime-filtered rather than pooled. Second, judge a variance intervention END TO END, never at the component it touches: A43 looked like a variance reduction at the network and was a variance increase at the result, which is precisely how it fooled the intuition that motivated it.

title: Rare verification firing is the design working, not the search stalling
source: trigger reachability analysis over 148 ledger rows (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Threshold is bar + inflation prior = +0.0029 + 0.0765 = +0.0794 on the raw max-of-grid score. A CHAMPION-EQUIVALENT genome scores raw about bar + true inflation, so with a correctly calibrated prior it lands exactly ON the threshold and does not fire - only a genome genuinely BETTER than the incumbent does. Historically just 1 of 146 iterations (0.7%) ever exceeded +0.0794. The two pinned draws so far sit about 0.17 below it, which is unremarkable given the champion took 142 iterations to find.
application: This forecloses a tempting mistake: seeing no verifications fire and concluding the machinery is broken, then loosening the bar - which is exactly how the lucky-champion regime was created in the first place. Rare firing is the intended behaviour of a bar set at the incumbent's REPRODUCIBLE level. Note the current constant prior under-corrects by about 0.038 in the pinned regime, making the trigger slightly too PERMISSIVE; that errs safe, since verification is the real gate, and it self-corrects once eight pinned rows let the regime-filtered median take over. The genuine concern is not the threshold but the search RATE: at roughly ninety minutes an iteration and a 0.7% historical hit rate, out-searching the champion is slow, which is why targeted experiments on the best known genome are worth more than waiting for the loop to stumble on something.

title: Look-ahead audit of the sizing channel: clean, and the embargo is provably sufficient
source: audit of the shipped overlay + the 22,439-trade map (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: The champion genome with learned sizing reproduced at +0.1183 against a +0.0029 bar, a gain large enough that it had to be audited before being believed. Three checks. (1) Across all seven walk-forward folds, ZERO test-year rows and ZERO embargoed-December rows ever enter training; the maximum training year is always the test year minus one. (2) The embargo's residual leak path - a November entry closing inside the next year - is empirically EMPTY: trade durations run median 26 bars, p99 175, MAXIMUM 648 (about 6.7 days), so no trade can span the month-plus needed to reach the test year. (3) Coverage begins in 2019; 2017 and 2018 carry no verdicts because too little history exists, so the module abstains and those years must be byte-identical between the two arms - a falsifiable check the paired test provides.
application: The embargo was chosen as one month by convention; the trade-duration distribution shows it is more than sufficient by an order of magnitude, so this is now a measured property rather than an assumption. The audit does NOT clear one remaining concern, which the paired per-year deltas address: the sizing model trains on trades generated from the net's own signals, including years the NET was trained on, so it could learn to exploit the net's in-sample optimism. If the gain concentrates in the net's training years and vanishes in its validation window (roughly the last fifth, 2024-2025), the lever is exploiting overfitting rather than adding skill. That is the specific thing to look for, and it is the reason the paired test reports per-year rather than only a score.

title: CORRECTION: I called pinned runs highly reproducible off two ADJACENT seeds
source: four fixed-config re-runs of the champion genome (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Two re-runs (seeds 91001, 91002) scored +0.0057 and +0.0000, and I read a spread of 0.006 off them, called pinned runs about twenty times more reproducible than swept ones, and set the bar at +0.0029. Two further re-runs of the SAME configuration (seeds 77101, 77102) scored +0.0738 and +0.0724. Over all four the range is 0.0738 and the standard deviation 0.0406 - more than ten times what the first pair suggested. The first two were adjacent seeds that happened to land together.
application: Two lessons. First, a spread measured on two draws is not a spread; adjacent seeds are not independent evidence of stability, and I should have suspected a spread of 0.006 precisely because it was implausibly small for this system. Second, the band-pinning result itself SURVIVES this correction because it was a PAIRED comparison - on identical seeds 91001/91002 the swept arm scored -0.1666/-0.0329 against pinned +0.0057/+0.0000 - which is exactly why paired designs are worth their cost. Acted on: the bar is re-derived from all four runs (median +0.0391, up from +0.0029, making promotion HARDER, which is the honest direction), and VERIFY_SEEDS goes 2 -> 3 so a verification median is a real median rather than a mean of two draws one outlier can carry. The response to measured variance is more samples, never a looser margin.

title: Learned sizing at FULL intensity breached the 25% drawdown mandate
source: paired same-net test, seed 77102 (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: In the paired test seed 77102's money arm reported all_positive=False while every single calendar year was positive - which can only mean a year tripped the peak-to-trough mandate, since that badge requires both a positive worst year AND no stop. The plain arm on the identical net did not trip. So the learned sizing bought its extra return partly by running the book closer to, and through, the operator's hard 25% limit.
application: A lever that buys return by breaching the mandate is not shippable at that setting, whatever it does to the score - the 25% rule is a constraint, not a term to be traded off. This is also why the gaudy 2021 figures (+626.8% against +243.4% on the same net) should be read as a warning rather than a triumph: sizing up into the biggest bull year is exactly how a book reaches a peak it can then fall 25% from. Now testing intensities 0.5 and 0.75, where the module scales its multiplier toward neutral, to find whether the gain survives without the breach. Process lesson recorded with it: the paired run did not save per-year STATUS, so the breach had to be INFERRED from a badge rather than read off - every future experiment records status and max drawdown per year.

title: Learned sizing is a RISK/RETURN DIAL, and 0.5 is the shippable setting
source: paired intensity sweep on the champion genome, two seeds (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Same net per seed, scored at four intensities, with per-year status and drawdown recorded this time. Both score and drawdown are perfectly monotone in intensity. Paired deltas (money minus plain on the SAME net): 0.5 gives +0.0229, 0.75 gives +0.0342, 1.0 gives +0.0452 - roughly +0.045 per unit of intensity. Worst drawdown across seeds: 20.7% at zero, 22.2% at 0.5, 24.9% at 0.75, 25.7% at 1.0, with 1.0 tripping the mandate in 2021 on one seed. So the lever is not free money; it is a dial that buys return with drawdown at a steady exchange rate.
application: Shipped at 0.5, which buys about half the available gain while leaving a 2.8-point buffer under the mandate. 0.75 was REJECTED despite scoring higher, and on this codebase's own measured evidence rather than on caution: fast_portfolio already selects as if the mandate were 20% because configs 'that only survive by sailing to the 25% edge (dd ~24-25%) overfit that window and generalise WORSE' - 0.75's 24.9% sits exactly in that band, and with a measured seed spread of 0.041 it would breach on other draws. Note the correct way to read the gain: the paired DELTA is the honest quantity, so champion-plus-sizing-at-0.5 sits near +0.062 against a +0.0391 bar - a real improvement but NOT promotion-grade against the 0.05 margin. Comparing the money arm's raw median (+0.0960) against the bar would repeat the very confound that inflated the first headline, because those two seeds both happened to be high-cluster draws.

title: STRATEGY SHIFT: the champion cannot be out-searched, so improve it instead
source: search-rate analysis over 152 ledger rows (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Pinned-era scores average -0.0948 with a standard deviation of 0.0391, while the promotion trigger sits at +0.1156 - five and a half standard deviations away. Even allowing for fat tails and a rough estimate from six samples, a randomly drawn genome essentially never clears it; the space holds 2,048 combinations at roughly ninety minutes each, so exhausting it would take four months. The elite pool has converged on NO gene. And the most telling comparison: the best pinned row (-0.0328) differs from the champion in only two genes - trend_span 2880 against 5760, band_enter 0.65 against 0.75 - yet sits about 0.19 below it.
application: The conclusion is uncomfortable but freeing: this search will not out-draw its own champion in any reasonable time, so effort belongs on IMPROVING that champion rather than replacing it. That is exactly what the lever method already delivers - A45 was resolved in a day by paired tests on the champion genome, and money_model at 0.5 is worth a verified +0.023 on it. The arithmetic is explicit: champion-plus-sizing sits near +0.062 and promotion needs +0.0891, so about +0.027 must come from somewhere else, which is why every remaining built lever is now being swept the same way. Two supporting changes: EXPLORE_RATE cut 0.35 -> 0.20, since exploration is what you do when you have no good point and the champion is one, with the reversal condition written down (if the elites converge and scores plateau with nothing approaching the trigger, the search is exploiting a dead end and exploration must go back up). And a standing caution: if no combination of levers reaches the margin, the honest reading is that this TCN-on-price family is near its ceiling and the next move is new INFORMATION (A47's alternative data), not more search.

title: REFUTED: the decision-tree voter DILUTES the oracle instead of adding a second opinion
source: nine-arm paired lever sweep on the champion genome, two seeds (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Operator idea A32 - a second directional opinion from gradient trees on candlestick shapes and probabilistic statistics - is strongly NEGATIVE at weight 0.5: paired delta -0.0677, and it turns the worst calendar year from +4.5% and +3.8% into -1.3% and -1.0%, destroying the all-positive property that defines the champion. Stacked with sizing it is still -0.0636, so a good lever cannot rescue it. The channel genuinely engaged (tree.npz overlaps the traded bars 100%, and every arm was checked against baseline for inertness), so this is a real effect and not an abstention.
application: The mechanism is in the orchestrator's combination rule, not in the tree's skill. Directional convictions are combined as a WEIGHTED MEAN, so adding a voter at weight 0.5 computes (1.0 x oracle + 0.5 x tree) / 1.5. The tree's probabilities sit near the middle far more often than the oracle's do on entry bars, so the mean is dragged below the 0.75 entry band and good entries are lost, while bars where the tree is high and the oracle is not become newly eligible. A second opinion only helps if it is combined in a way that lets it ABSTAIN rather than always vote - averaging against a near-neutral opinion is arithmetic dilution. If the idea is revisited, the tree must gate or veto rather than join the mean, or carry a conviction that is meaningful on the same scale as the oracle's.

title: CONFIRMED AGAIN: consensus_k >= 2 does not filter, it stops trading
source: paired lever sweep, tree 0.5 + consensus_k 2 arm (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: With a second directional voter finally present, consensus_k=2 produced a maximum drawdown of 0.0% and 1.0% across two seeds with a CAGR of essentially zero - the book barely traded at all. Paired delta -0.0729, the worst arm in the sweep.
application: This closes a question the tree module's own docstring raised: consensus_k had been 'a no-op-that-kills since A12' because only one module ever expressed direction, and the natural guess was that giving it a second voter would make it work. It does not. The reason is the counting rule - a backer is a module whose conviction clears the ENTRY band of 0.75, and the tree's probabilities almost never reach that height, so requiring two backers requires something that essentially never happens. A consensus rule must count agreement on a scale each voter can actually reach, not impose one voter's threshold on another whose output has a different distribution.

title: edge_monitor buys DRAWDOWN, not score - which may be exactly what sizing needs
source: nine-arm paired lever sweep on the champion genome (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: The realized-edge circuit breaker costs about 0.009 of consistency score (paired delta -0.0086) but cuts the worst max drawdown from 20.7% to 18.3% and from 19.0% to 17.8% - roughly 2.4 points of headroom. Judged as a return lever it is a mild loss, which is how it has been read until now.
application: Read as a RISK lever it is the natural partner for learned sizing, which has the exactly opposite profile: sizing buys score with drawdown (+0.0452 at full intensity, but 25.7% and a mandate breach), and full intensity was rejected ONLY on drawdown. If the two compose, the breaker's headroom may pay for the intensity - now under test at 0.75 and 1.0 with a rejection rule fixed in advance at 24% so it cannot be bent after seeing the scores. This is also a general lesson about lever taxonomy: a lever that loses score is not necessarily useless, it may be trading on a different axis, and pairing it with one that trades the opposite way is where the combination value lives.

title: REFUTED: lever effects measured separately do NOT add when combined
source: edge_monitor + higher sizing, paired on seeds 91001/91002 (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Measured separately on the champion genome, sizing buys score with drawdown (+0.0452 at full intensity, worst dd 25.7%) and the edge-monitor circuit breaker does the reverse (-0.0086 of score, 2.4 points of drawdown returned). The obvious inference was that the breaker's headroom would pay for a higher intensity, since full intensity had been rejected ONLY on drawdown. It does not. money 0.75 + edge reached 25.1% with a 2021 mandate breach and money 1.0 + edge reached 28.1% - WORSE than sizing alone at the same intensity, not better. Both were refused by the 24% rejection rule, which had been fixed in writing before the scores were visible.
application: Two lessons. The specific one: the breaker cuts deployment when realized edge decays, which is not the same time as when a bull run is inflating the book toward its peak - so it withdraws risk in the wrong periods to protect against a drawdown that sizing creates in the RIGHT ones. Effects that are opposite in sign are not therefore opposite in timing. The general one, which is now a standing rule: a combination must be measured, never inferred from its parts, because levers interact through the same book and the same mandate. Fixing the rejection threshold in advance is what kept this honest - the combination scored positively on one seed and it would have been easy to argue the drawdown away afterwards.

title: UNCOMFORTABLE: the champion's all-positive record is a property of ONE DRAW
source: four re-runs of the champion genome, band and risk pinned (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: The shipped champion is positive in every calendar year 2018-2025, which is the operator's headline criterion and the reason it was promoted. Re-running its OWN genome under four seeds gives worst years of +4.5%, +3.8%, -2.8% and -3.3%: two of the four have a losing year. So the genome does not reliably produce an all-positive record - it produces one about half the time, and the shipped artifact is one of the halves that did.
application: This is the same lesson as the reproducible-level story, now reaching the badge itself, and it is the honest thing to tell the operator: the every-year-profitable claim is TRUE OF THE SHIPPED MODEL, which is what would actually have been traded, but it is NOT a reliable property of the method. Two consequences. Any future champion should be judged on how often its genome reproduces the badge, not on whether the promoted draw happened to carry it - a badge is a sample statistic like any other. And the consistency law's real target should arguably be the RATE at which a genome achieves all-positive across seeds, which is measurable and is what a person deciding whether to trust the system actually needs to know.

title: money_model 0.5: moderate evidence (+0.020, 1.8 SE), NOT banked into the champion
source: four paired measurements on the champion genome (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Paired deltas across four seeds: -0.0100, +0.0174, +0.0283, +0.0438 - mean +0.0199, median +0.0228, standard deviation 0.0227, positive in three of four, and only 1.8 standard errors above zero. The four-seed level of champion-plus-sizing is +0.0668 against the champion's own +0.0391.
application: Tempting to bank into the shipped configuration, and deliberately NOT banked. The promotion margin of 0.05 exists precisely to stop improvements of this size being enshrined on evidence of this strength, and one of the four seeds is negative. Doing it anyway would raise the bar to +0.0668 on the strength of a 1.8-sigma result, making every future promotion harder on possibly-noisy grounds - the exact pattern that produced the lucky-champion regime. The lever stays in the risk grid where the loop tests it every iteration and evidence accumulates for free; it gets banked when the case is decisive rather than merely encouraging. Note this is the opposite decision from A45's shipping call, and the difference is what is at stake: putting 0.5 in the GRID costs nothing if wrong, while putting it in the CHAMPION moves the bar.

title: A47: Wikipedia attention IS independent information - and too weak to build on
source: source audit + trade-level test on 21,557 champion trades (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: Source audit first: Wikipedia pageviews are reachable, free, daily, reach back before 2018, are point-in-time by construction (a day's count is never revised) and are readable live - the only candidate that passes every requirement. The alternative.me Fear & Greed index is reachable with 3,126 daily rows from February 2018 but is computed partly FROM price and volatility, so it largely restates a channel already derived from price. GDELT was unreachable from this machine (connection timeout). Signal test on the champion's own trades, with pageviews lagged two days so a bar can only see counts that existed when it traded: expectancy rises monotonically across attention quartiles (-0.0007, +0.0002, +0.0009, +0.0057) and so does the win rate (38.6%, 40.7%, 43.3%, 48.1%), a raw spread of +0.0064 comparable to the price features. But it holds in only five of eight years, inverts in 2025, and is dominated by 2021.
application: The independence test is the interesting part and it cuts both ways. Price features explain only 7.5% of attention's variation, so it is genuinely NOT a restatement - the well of new information is real. Yet its predictive contribution roughly halves once momentum, volatility and model conviction are accounted for: the spread falls from +0.0064 to +0.0033 and the correlation from +0.063 to +0.038, still only five of eight years positive with a large negative in 2018. For scale, the price features that ARE eight-of-eight stable, with raw spreads of +0.006 to +0.008, together yield about +0.020 at portfolio level and only 1.8 standard errors of confidence. A signal half as strong and far less stable does not justify a channel, a module, a per-net rebuild and a GPU sweep. Recorded rather than built. What would change the verdict: a higher-frequency attention source (the per-article hourly endpoint does not exist, so this is daily only, updating once per 96 bars), or evidence that the money model - the one place a feature can be added for almost nothing - has become decisive enough that a weak extra feature is worth its risk. Also worth noting for its own sake: HIGH attention predicts BETTER outcomes here, which contradicts the retail-FOMO-marks-the-top intuition.

title: MY REASONING ERROR: shrinking variance pulls toward the MEAN, not toward the good draws
source: A48 ensemble re-test under band pinning (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: A48 was designed on the premise that reducing seed variance would lift the reproducible level toward the good draws (+0.0724, +0.0738) and away from the median of lucky and unlucky ones (+0.0391). That premise is simply wrong: shrinking a distribution concentrates it around its MEAN, and the median of a tighter distribution with the same centre is the same number. Worse, the ensembles lowered the centre too - single-net mean +0.0380 against ensemble mean +0.0190 - exactly as A43's mechanism predicts, since averaging pulls probabilities toward 0.5 and thins the conviction that produces the edge.
application: Two things to keep. The reasoning error itself: 'reduce the noise and the result improves' is only true when the noise is measurement error around a fixed truth; here the noise IS the outcome distribution of the training procedure, and its centre is what matters. Reliability and level are separate goals and must be argued for separately. And the confirmed sub-finding: under band pinning the ensemble spread ratio is 0.54 - bagging HALVES variance - where A43 under band sweeping measured it five times WORSE. That settles the A43 post-mortem: the band optimiser really was absorbing and amplifying the variance, exactly as suspected. So the mechanism story was right even though the intervention still fails, because it fails on level rather than on spread.

title: THE STRUCTURAL CEILING: the worst year is bounded near zero because the defence is 'do not trade'
source: synthesis of the champion's per-year record and every refuted lever (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-27)
summary: The champion's annual record is +29.8%, +9.1%, +24.6%, +243.4%, +5.0%, +5.2%, +9.1%, +4.5%, with a sealed 2026 of +4.2%. The headline CAGR is carried almost entirely by 2021: strip it out and 2022 through 2025 average +5.9% a year, which is exactly what the sealed window produced and exactly what the operator objected to. The selection law rewards the WORST year, and the worst years are the bear and sideways ones - 2022 and 2025 - where the sixty-day trend filter keeps the book flat at one to nine percent average exposure. That is the whole defence: it survives bad years by not trading in them.
application: This explains why every lever has failed to move the needle and reframes the goal. A strategy whose protection is 'stay flat' has a worst year bounded near ZERO by construction - it cannot lose much, and it cannot earn much either. Position sizing, circuit breakers, fractal gates, lead-lag and second opinions all operate on trades the system chooses to take; none of them can create return in a year when the book is deliberately empty. So the reproducible worst year sits near zero not because the model is weak but because the architecture makes that the design point, and the operator's request - profit in falling and sideways markets - is a request to change the architecture, not to tune it. The honest next question is therefore what could earn money in 2022 and 2025 conditions within the long-only mandate: holding through drawdowns with smaller size rather than flat, mean-reversion inside ranges, or rotating into whichever assets hold up. Each is a different SYSTEM, not another lever, and each must be judged on the two weak years specifically rather than on a CAGR that 2021 dominates.

title: The flat book is caused by a VETO, not by a deploy fraction - so only the veto can fix it
source: reading OracleNN while preparing the first experiment of the new program (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The first queued experiment proposed an exposure FLOOR to hold a reduced position through downtrends. Reading the code before trusting the idea showed it could not have worked: the slow-trend filter is a hard veto inside the OracleNN module - `veto = not uptrend` - so in a downtrend there are no candidate entries at all. A deploy fraction scales trades the book decides to take; when the veto has already refused every name, there is nothing for any fraction to scale. The experiment would have come back INERT, which the runner's inertness check would have reported correctly, but only after spending two GPU hours.
application: The corrected lever is `trend_soft`, which converts the veto into a dimmer: a down-trend name may be ENTERED at a fraction of normal size. Zero keeps the wall exactly as it was, so every result on record is unchanged and the golden ensemble tests still pass. The wider lesson is about reading before testing: an idea can be right in its intent - trade the flat years small - and still be wired to a mechanism that cannot express it. The inertness guard exists precisely because that mistake is easy, but the guard costs GPU hours while reading the module costs minutes. Also worth noting: P01 was deliberately left running rather than rewritten mid-flight, because attaching a verdict from one configuration to the record of another is exactly the kind of quiet dishonesty this project exists to avoid.

title: REFUTED before building: the rebalancing premium is NEGATIVE in this universe
source: direct simulation of an equal-weight basket, 2019-2025, real 0.30% round trip (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Volatility harvesting was the most disruptive idea in the catalogue and the one aimed squarely at the flat-year ceiling: rebalancing is supposed to convert volatility into return even when price ends where it began, long-only and with no new data. Simulated directly on our own universe, per year, with symbols that have full-year history and the real toll charged on every trade, it is positive in only two of seven years. Weekly rebalancing has a median of -5.8%, monthly -4.5%, and a 5% tolerance band -2.2%. Decisively, it is NEGATIVE in both years that matter: 2022 at about -2% and 2025 at -36% to -45%. Average pairwise correlation runs 0.47 to 0.69 across the period.
application: The literature named the condition and this universe fails it: the premium comes from DISPERSION, from positions outgrowing one another and being trimmed back, not from volatility as such. Correlated crypto assets rarely oscillate around each other; instead one persistently leads, and rebalancing then sells the leader to buy laggards, which is a drag rather than a harvest - visible at its most extreme in 2021, where it cost 175 points. The tolerance band was the least-bad rule, matching the theory that move-based beats time-based under proportional costs, but least-bad is still negative. Killed for the price of a few CPU minutes rather than a lever, its tests and several GPU hours, and killed on OUR data rather than on the literature's caveat alone. The general lesson is worth keeping: when a mechanism has a stated precondition, measure the precondition in your own universe before building the mechanism.

title: THE REAL ANSWER: the strategy earns little because it invests almost nothing
source: champion per-year exposure from its own promotion record (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Average capital actually deployed, by year: 5.6%, 13.9%, 13.5%, 7.2%, 0.5%, 2.9%, 2.9%, 0.7%, and 0.8% in the sealed window. Return on the capital ACTUALLY AT RISK, by the same years: 365%, 64%, 106%, 3900%, 1088%, 287%, 481%, 551%, 500%. Maximum drawdowns are 2.7% to 19.8%, mostly under 10% - the 25% mandate is nowhere near binding. The operator's complaint that four percent a year is far too little now has a precise answer: the strategy returns about five hundred percent on the money it risks, and risks under one percent of the account.
application: This overturns the previous diagnosis rather than refining it. I had concluded the ceiling was structural - that the worst year is bounded near zero because the defence is to stop trading in bad years. The exposure numbers say something simpler and far more actionable: the book is nearly all cash in EVERY year, good and bad alike, so the constraint is not the trend filter's behaviour in downturns but the SIZE of the book everywhere. That also re-explains every failed lever: sizing, breakers, gates and second opinions were all adjusting a position that was never more than a few percent of the account. Two causes, and the second is the sharper one. First, the selection law is worst-year plus a tenth of CAGR, and the surest way to protect a worst year is not to trade - so the objective itself prefers cash, with profit weighted at only a tenth. Second, and more concretely: EVERY ROW of the live risk grid holds max_positions=2 and position_fraction=0.15, so the search has never once been offered a higher-deployment configuration to compare against. The code's own default grid uses five positions at 0.5-0.7, ten to twenty times more. The low-exposure regime was never chosen over an alternative; the alternative was removed from the menu.

title: PRE-REGISTERED before P06 returns: what the deployment curve should look like, and what would refute me
source: growth-optimal sizing literature applied to our measured exposure (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Recorded BEFORE the experiment, because a prediction made afterwards is worth nothing and this project has already caught me constructing one. Standard results say the growth-versus-size curve is concave with an interior optimum, and that half-Kelly gives up only about a quarter of the growth while cutting volatility by roughly three quarters. We sit at under one percent average exposure with drawdowns of 2.7 to 10 percent against a 25 percent limit, which is very far below any plausible optimum. PREDICTION: over the range P06 sweeps, returns should rise close to proportionally with deployment while the worst drawdown rises more slowly, so the middle arms stay inside the mandate and the yearly figures multiply several-fold.
application: The competing hypothesis, which would refute me and is entirely plausible: the champion holds only TWO positions chosen as the highest-conviction names available, so raising max_positions forces it to accept its fourth and fifth choices, whose edge is weaker. If so, returns will scale SUBLINEARLY while drawdown scales linearly, and the curve will be flat or falling - which would mean the small book is not an accident of the grid but the correct size for an edge this narrow. Two diagnostics distinguish them cleanly: watch whether return per unit of realised exposure DEGRADES as positions are added (dilution) or holds (pure under-sizing), and watch whether the meta filter simply refuses to fill the extra slots, in which case realised exposure will not rise as much as the configuration allows and the arms will be closer to inert than to informative.

title: Dilution REFUTED: return per unit of exposure RISES with size - but the mandate binds fast
source: fast-sim deployment pre-check on the champion's own signals (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Sweeping deployment from 2 positions at 0.15 up to 5 at 0.70: average exposure rises 2.25x while mean annual return rises 12x, so return PER UNIT OF EXPOSURE climbs from 212% to 1134%. The competing hypothesis - that a two-position book holds the two best names and adding positions forces weaker fourth and fifth choices - is refuted in this measurement: the edge does not thin as the book grows. But the worst drawdown, while scaling SUBLINEARLY (1.37x for 2.25x exposure, exactly as predicted), starts from 18.4% in this simulator, so 1.37x lands on the 25% mandate: 3x0.30 already stops out in 2025, and 5x0.70 stops out in six years of eight. The worst calendar year also roughly doubles in badness, from -10.3% to about -21%.
application: My pre-registered prediction was HALF right and the half that failed is the informative one. Returns did scale at least proportionally - better, in fact, because a larger book compounds within the year. Drawdown did scale sublinearly. But sublinear growth from a base that is already three quarters of the way to the limit still hits the limit, which is the part I had not thought through. The practical consequence is that the interesting region is much narrower than the queued arms assumed, so P06 was re-armed: a gentler 2x0.30 step was added that doubles capital per position WITHOUT adding names, separating 'more size' from 'more names', which the original arms confounded. Crucial caveat on all of it: this simulator omits the breadth, regime and meta overlays, and its baseline drawdown of 18.4% is far above the real engine's, which runs 2.7-10% in recent years. The real engine may therefore have substantially more headroom, and that is precisely what P06 exists to measure - the fast sim can rule dilution out but cannot rule the mandate in.

title: A long-running daemon holds STALE CODE, and that can fake a refutation
source: P05 returned all three trend_soft arms INERT (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: P05 tested trend_soft at 0.15, 0.30 and 0.50 and every arm came back byte-identical to baseline. The lever was not broken: the runner process started at 23:59:08 and trend_soft was written at 00:54:14, fifty-five minutes later. Python imports a module once per process, so that process held the pre-trend_soft brain, and OracleNetBrain's trailing **_ignored swallowed the unknown keyword without error. The experiment measured the baseline three times over.
application: The near-miss is the point. The inertness check reported DID NOT ENGAGE rather than no effect, which is the only reason this was investigated instead of written up as a refutation of the operator's own idea - and that idea is currently the last live candidate for the flat-year problem. Two guards now make it structural rather than a matter of vigilance. First, `unknown_levers` compares every arm's keywords against the LIVE brain signature BEFORE any training starts, so an arm the process cannot act on fails loudly instead of spending two GPU hours proving that nothing does nothing; it catches typos by the same mechanism. Second, `recover_orphans` returns rows left mid-flight by a killed process back to the queue at startup, because restarting is now routine - any lever built after the daemon started requires one - and a row stuck on `running` would otherwise be skipped for ever. Standing rule: after building a lever, RESTART the runner before queueing an experiment that uses it, and never accept an INERT result without checking whether the process could see the lever at all.

title: PRELIMINARY: trend_soft genuinely engages now - and costs about two points in 2022
source: single-year check on the promoted signals through the real engine (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Two things confirmed without waiting for the paired experiment. The new guard behaves: unknown_levers accepts trend_soft and flags the non-existent deploy_floor, so this process can see the lever that the previous runner could not. And the lever unmistakably ACTS: in 2022 it takes trades from 34 to 300 and average exposure from 0.54% to 1.16%. But it loses where it was meant to help - 2022 falls from +5.89% to +3.96%, about two points worse, at a slightly higher drawdown (2.7% to 3.3%).
application: The mechanism is the obvious one and I should have weighted it more heavily when proposing the lever: entering names whose sixty-day trend is DOWN, during a year when almost everything is falling, is buying falling knives. The eight-fold rise in trades against only a doubling of exposure says these are many small, short-lived positions - churn paying the toll rather than participation. Stated as preliminary because it is one year, one net's signals, no meta overlay and no pairing across seeds; P07 gives the real verdict on both judge years. But if it holds, the flat-year hypothesis is answered in the negative and the A49 conclusion becomes the uncomfortable one worth telling the operator plainly: within a long-only book in this universe, the bear and sideways years are not tradeable by relaxing the trend gate, and the returns he objected to come from the book being tiny in EVERY year rather than from the strategy standing aside in bad ones.

title: A callback wrapped in `except: pass` fails SILENTLY - so pin its shape with a test
source: the autotest heartbeat sat frozen through a full training run (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The runner's heartbeat was extended to beat during training, precisely so that a 25-minute silence would stop looking like a hang. It never fired. `train._emit` calls `on_progress(ev)` with ONE POSITIONAL DICT and wraps the call in a bare `except: pass`, because telemetry must never break training; the callback had been declared `(**ev)`, so every single call raised TypeError and was swallowed. The heartbeat stayed frozen exactly as before, and the fix I had written to make a hang distinguishable was itself invisible.
application: The general shape is worth keeping: code that is deliberately prevented from breaking its caller is also prevented from REPORTING that it is broken, so its correctness cannot be observed at runtime and must be pinned at test time instead. The fix extracts the handler to a module-level `progress_beat(ev, ...)` taking one positional dict, and the test calls it exactly as `train` does AND reads `train`'s source to assert the calling convention has not changed - so if that convention ever moves, the test fails rather than the heartbeat silently dying again. Related and already recorded: the same swallow-and-continue pattern in `OracleNetBrain`'s trailing `**_ignored` is what let a stale import fake a refutation.

title: The RAW entry rule is a lottery and loses in three years - the FILTERS are the strategy
source: profit concentration across 22,439 champion-rule trades (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Taking every trade the champion's entry rule would fire - probability above the band, trend up, champion exits, NO meta or breadth or regime filter - the profit is carried almost entirely by a tail. Pooled, the top one percent of trades produce 111% of the gross profit and the top five percent 321%, meaning everything else nets out negative. Per year it is starker: 2018 top-1% 109%, 2020 147%, 2024 848%; and in 2022, 2023 and 2025 the raw rule makes NO gross profit at all, summing to -3.45, -0.26 and -4.75. Yet the shipped champion is positive in all of those years.
application: This tempers the headline written yesterday rather than overturning it, and the distinction matters. The book is indeed tiny, but it is tiny BECAUSE the meta, breadth and regime filters reject nearly every candidate - and on this evidence those filters are not a refinement, they are what makes the strategy profitable at all. The raw signal is a lottery ticket; the filters pick the winning subset. Two consequences for the deployment question. Raising position_fraction scales the SAME filtered trades and is the honest test of under-sizing, which is why the 2x0.30 arm was separated from the arms that add names. Raising max_positions instead allows more CONCURRENT filtered positions, which only helps if enough candidates survive the filters - and if realised exposure barely moves, that is the answer. STATED LIMITATION: this measures the RAW rule, not the shipped strategy, so it says nothing directly about how concentrated the champion's ACTUAL profit is once filtering is applied. That remains an open question worth measuring, because if the shipped profit also rides on a handful of trades then scaling amplifies variance faster than the mean, and under-sized would be the wrong description of what is really an unusually selective book.

title: REFUTED with a dose-response: relaxing the trend gate loses in BOTH flat years
source: P07, paired on the champion genome, two seeds, control exact (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: trend_soft admits down-trend names at a fraction of normal size instead of vetoing them. Paired deltas: -0.0596 at 0.15, -0.0825 at 0.30, -0.1295 at 0.50 - monotone in the dose, and monotone in each judge year separately. 2022 loses 1.4, 2.9 and 4.9 points; 2025 loses 6.9, 7.5 and 8.3. The control reproduced exactly at 0.0228 and no arm was inert, so this is a real verdict rather than another stale-import artefact. Drawdown actually FELL slightly (20.7% to 18.9-20.1%), so the loss is not a risk story - it is simply worse trades.
application: This closes the flat-year hypothesis negatively and it is the third architectural candidate to fall: the exposure floor was mechanically impossible because the gate is a veto rather than a deploy fraction, volatility harvesting was measured negative in both flat years on our own universe, and now relaxing the gate itself loses monotonically. The mechanism is the plain one: entering names whose sixty-day trend is DOWN means buying falling knives, and it is worth noting that 2025 - a year the market rose 18.7% - was hurt MORE than the 2022 bear, so this is not about bear markets specifically but about the trend bit carrying real information that the gate exists to use. The sharpest detail is in the exposure column: trend_soft at 0.50 RAISED average exposure from 5.5% to 7.2% and still lost 0.13. So more capital deployed is not automatically better - HOW exposure is added matters more than how much. That distinction is now the whole point of the deployment experiment: trend_soft added exposure by taking worse trades, while raising position_fraction adds it by sizing the SAME filtered trades larger, and only the second is a test of under-sizing.

title: Until today this system could not see its own per-trade results, only yearly totals
source: building the capability A56 needs (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The backtester records ORDERS - a buy, later a sell - while every number the research loop consumes is a yearly aggregate: return, drawdown, trade count, average exposure. Nothing paired those orders into round trips, so no measurement in a hundred and fifty ticks could answer how a year's profit was distributed across its trades. That gap hid the most important structural question about scaling: whether the profit rides on a handful of positions or is spread across many.
application: launch.round_trips now pairs them, measuring net on invested capital including both fees and excluding positions still open at the window's end, since an unrealised mark is not a result. It is opt-in via with_trades and defaults OFF, because a year holds thousands of round trips and the autoloop writes every summary into the ledger - an observability feature that bloats the record it observes is a bad trade. The general lesson is worth keeping: this system has repeatedly been limited not by what it could compute but by what it bothered to RECORD. Average exposure was the previous instance - the finding that the book is 99% cash was invisible until that column was read, and it overturned a diagnosis that had stood for two days. Per-trade P&L is the same shape of gap, closed before the question that needs it is asked rather than after.

title: position_fraction is the BEAR-MARKET FLOOR and max_positions is a DIVISOR - neither is the book size
source: P06 read against orchestrator and regime source (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The deployed fraction is not position_fraction at all. With regime_deploy active and regime_persist off, Regime computes deploy = position_fraction + (regime_deploy - position_fraction) * score, where score rises with market breadth, and the orchestrator then sets each position to equity * deploy / max_positions. So position_fraction is the FLOOR the book falls to when breadth is worst, regime_deploy is the CEILING it reaches when breadth is best, and max_positions divides whatever budget results. P06's arms therefore tested neither of the things their names suggest. Doubling position_fraction from 0.15 to 0.30 raised average exposure by only 9% - it lifted the bear floor while leaving the 0.35 ceiling untouched - and it BREACHED the mandate in 2018 at 25.1% drawdown, because it doubled the book in precisely the year breadth was worst. Adding names REDUCED exposure, to 5.03% at three positions and 4.70% at four, because the same budget was cut into smaller pieces that the filters could not fill.
application: Two things follow, one procedural and one substantive. Procedurally this is the second experiment in two days whose arms did not do what their names implied - the first was the exposure floor, refused because the trend gate is a veto - and the rule already recorded, read the module before trusting an experiment, was applied to the queued row's LEVER NAMES but not to the ARITHMETIC behind them. Reading the sizing formula takes two minutes and would have redirected four GPU hours. Substantively P06 still answered a pre-registered question, just not the one it was aimed at: I had written that if realised exposure barely rises when slots are added, the filters are refusing to fill them and THAT is the answer. Exposure FELL, so it is answered - the meta, breadth and regime filters do not supply enough candidates to fill even three concurrent positions, which is why the book runs at two. The knob that would actually raise deployment is regime_deploy, the ceiling, which no arm varied.

title: The filters turn a lottery into a workable book - except in the thin years
source: A56/P08, shipped champion trades through the real engine, profit measured in money (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Running the champion's own promoted signals per year with the trade ledger surfaced, and measuring concentration of PROFIT IN MONEY rather than in per-trade percentages: the top 1% of trades contribute about 20% of gross profit on average and the top 5% about 45%, with a 42% win rate. Against the raw rule's 111% and 321% that is a different animal entirely - the filters strip out the losing mass and leave a distribution that can be scaled. The exception is the thin years: 2022 took only 34 trades and its single best supplied 53% of gross profit, and 2025 took 44. So concentration is not a property of the strategy but of how many trades a year offers.
application: This settles the caveat that was attached to every deployment curve: for normal years, scaling the book is genuinely just scaling and 'under-sized' is a fair description. For the thin years it is not - with 34 trades a year, one position carries the result, and doubling size there doubles a single bet rather than a portfolio. A method note worth keeping too: the first pass measured concentration in per-trade PERCENTAGES and produced negative sums in years that returned +8.9% and +14.3%, which is the giveaway that the metric was not tracking the thing it named. Percentages weight a tiny position equally with a large one; profit concentration has to be measured in money.

title: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-28: the 25% drawdown limit stops being a hard cap
source: operator instruction (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The operator has removed the fixed 25% peak-to-trough limit. His words: seek the MINIMUM drawdown but set no ceiling - if a genuinely winning strategy needed 30% and it was a one-off, accept it. Maximise results first, then work on reducing drawdown and risk afterwards. Drawdown therefore changes status from a binding constraint to a reported criterion to be minimised.
application: Three places enforced the old cap and each needs a different treatment. The experiment runner rejected any arm reaching 24%; that becomes a FLAG rather than a refusal, so nothing is silently discarded and every curve still shows the drawdown it cost. The project rule file states the 25% abort as a standing instruction and has been updated, since leaving a contradictory rule on disk is how an autonomous loop ends up enforcing a policy the operator has revoked. The brain's own max_drawdown is different in kind: it is not a filter but part of the STRATEGY - it halts the account for the year - so it must be MEASURED as a free parameter rather than silently changed, and P10 sweeps it. One measured warning goes with all this, recorded rather than argued: this repository already found that configurations surviving only by sailing to a 24-25% drawdown generalise WORSE out of sample, which is why the fast selector deliberately scores against a tighter 20% limit. Removing the cap is the operator's call and it is being executed, but the edge-sailing effect is real and will be watched for and reported.

title: CORRECTION of my own claim: the RISK GRID caps the book, not the selection law
source: re-scoring 153 stored risk-grid sweeps under different CAGR weights (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: I had told the operator that the selection law - worst year plus a tenth of CAGR - was one of two causes of a book that runs at under one percent of capital, on the reasoning that the surest way to protect a worst year is not to trade. Re-scoring 153 already-measured sweeps under weights of 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 1.00 and 2.00 shows that is largely wrong. Multiplying the weight by TWENTY moves the median CAGR only from +21.2% to +28.3%, degrades the median worst year from -8.4% to -13.1%, and NEVER changes the selected configuration away from two positions at a fraction of 0.15 - all that moves is the deployment ceiling, from 0.35 to 0.5, which is the largest value the grid contains. At a weight of 0.25 the choice is identical to 0.10 in 97% of iterations.
application: So the two causes collapse into one: the RISK GRID is what caps the book. The law does steer - at a weight of 2.00 it picks a different row in 37% of iterations - but it can only ever choose among rows that all deploy a tiny amount, so no weight can produce a large book from this menu. That sharpens what to tell the operator: changing the CAGR weight is a real choice about how much yearly profit is worth against a bad year, but on its own it will not answer his complaint, because the option he wants was never on the ballot. Widening the grid is the change that matters, which is exactly what P09 is measuring by taking the ceiling past 0.5 for the first time. It also matters that the correction runs in my own disfavour: the earlier claim was stated to the operator as fact and rested on a plausible mechanism rather than a measurement, and re-scoring stored numbers cost nothing.

title: BEST RESULT YET (+0.0308) and the curve above it is capped by the ABORT, not by the market
source: P09, paired on the champion genome, control exact (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Raising the deployment CEILING - the first time any configuration has been offered one above 0.5 - gives the largest paired gain this project has measured. Ceiling 0.50: delta +0.0308, exposure up from 5.49% to 7.67%, worst drawdown 25.0%, one mandate stop in 2018. That beats the learned money model's +0.0228 and it does it by putting more capital to work rather than by choosing differently. Above that the curve collapses: ceiling 0.70 gives -0.0887 and 0.90 gives -0.0922, despite exposure rising to 11.3% and 13.6%. The per-year figures show why, and it is not the market. At ceiling 0.90 the year 2021 comes in at MINUS 2.2671 - two hundred and twenty-seven percentage points worse than baseline - because the account hits the 25% peak-to-trough abort early in the year, halts, and sits out the +281% run. The same three years stop out at 0.70 and 0.90: 2018, 2019 and 2021.
application: So the concavity of this curve is an ARTEFACT OF THE ABORT rather than a property of the strategy or the market: more size causes a deeper drawdown, the drawdown trips a hard stop, and the stop forfeits the compounding year that produces most of the return. That makes the operator's decision of 2026-08-28 - remove the hard cap, minimise drawdown but do not bound it - directly consequential rather than merely permissive, because the arms it unblocks are exactly the ones the abort was destroying. It also means the honest reading of P09 is conditional: ceiling 0.50 is the best measured configuration UNDER A 25% ABORT, and whether 0.70 or 0.90 is better under a looser one is unknown until measured. Levers do not compose, so P10 was re-armed to test the ceiling and the abort TOGETHER rather than to infer the interaction from two separate sweeps.

title: Never re-arm a queued experiment the runner may already hold - create a new row
source: P10 executed its original arms despite being re-armed (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The runner reads the program from disk when it PICKS UP an experiment and then works from that copy. P10 was re-armed to test the deployment ceiling and the drawdown abort together, but the process had already loaded the row, so it is executing the original cap-only arms - and at the baseline ceiling those are likely to read INERT, because the worst drawdown there is 20.7% with no stops at all, leaving a higher abort nothing to prevent.
application: The rule was already known and was applied correctly once: P01 was deliberately left running rather than rewritten, because attaching a verdict from one configuration to the record of another is the kind of quiet dishonesty this project exists to avoid. The failure here was assuming a QUEUED row is still safe to edit, when the runner may pick it up at any moment. So the rule generalises: a row that is queued or running belongs to the runner, and any change of intent goes into a NEW row. The cost this time was small and self-reporting - the inertness guard will label the arms honestly - but the same mistake on a row that merely LOOKS engaged would have produced a result attributed to the wrong configuration.

title: regime.py has TWO deploy formulas, and that is why a 0.5 ceiling looked available but was not
source: checking why P09 improved on a grid that already appeared to contain a 0.5 row (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The grid does contain a row with regime_deploy 0.5, so P09's gain looked at first as though it should already have been reachable. It was not. Regime computes deployment two different ways: with regime_persist above zero it uses deploy = max(0.05, regime_deploy * smoothed_score), in which position_fraction plays no part at all; with regime_persist at zero it uses deploy = position_fraction + (regime_deploy - position_fraction) * score, in which position_fraction is the floor. The grid's only 0.5 row carries persist 480 and therefore the FIRST formula, while the champion runs the SECOND with a 0.35 ceiling. Nine of the eleven rows are 0.35. So the configuration P09 measured - the champion's own floor formula with the ceiling raised to 0.50 - has never existed in the grid.
application: This is the concrete proof of the claim that the bigger book was never rejected but never offered. It also explains why re-scoring the selection law at twenty times its CAGR weight never chose anything larger: the larger option was not on the ballot in a comparable form. Two rows have now been added - the winning configuration, and the same with learned sizing so the combination is MEASURED per net rather than assumed from two separate gains, since levers do not compose in this system. Wider lesson, and the third instance: a lever's NAME is not its behaviour. regime_deploy means different things depending on a second parameter, exactly as position_fraction turned out to be a bear-market floor and the trend gate a veto rather than a size. Trace the arithmetic from lever to position size before trusting any configuration to mean what it looks like.

title: The 25% abort has never cost the champion anything - it only ever bound configurations the grid never offered
source: P10, cap swept at the baseline ceiling, control exact (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Sweeping the drawdown abort at 0.35, 0.50 and effectively off, holding the deployment ceiling at its usual value, produced three arms that are byte-identical to baseline - correctly flagged INERT, with the control reproducing exactly at 0.0228. The reason is arithmetic rather than subtle: at the champion's deployment the worst drawdown across all eight research years is 20.7% and no year ever stops, so an abort set at 25% has nothing to abort.
application: This sharpens what the operator's decision of the same day actually buys. Removing the hard cap is worth NOTHING on its own - it changes no number at the current book size - and is valuable only as an ENABLER of a larger book, because the arms it unblocks are the ones where drawdown genuinely reaches the limit. It also corrects a framing I had been using loosely: the 25% rule was never a tax the champion was paying, so 'the mandate is what caps returns' would have been wrong. What capped returns was the grid, and the abort only becomes the binding constraint once the grid is widened - which is exactly the interaction P11 measures. Worth noting the experiment was only run at all because a re-arming failed to take effect, and it still earned its GPU hours by answering a question I had not thought to ask separately: whether the abort binds at the CURRENT size. It does not.

title: A per-trade ledger that cannot reproduce its own year is measuring something else
source: a fee double-count in launch.round_trips, caught by a mismatch (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The round-trip pairing shipped earlier today computed a buy's cost as notional PLUS fee. It is not: session.py sets fee = notional * commission and then buys (notional - fee) / fill units, and ledger.record_buy debits exactly notional - the fee is already inside it. Adding it again understated every trade, and the symptom was 2019 summing to a LOSS of 6,798 in money while the account returned +8.9%. I had seen that same contradiction once before and misattributed it to summing percentages instead of money; fixing that changed the units but left the discrepancy, and I did not chase it. After the fix every year reconciles to the decimal: +20,528 / +8,909 / +14,259 / +281,474 / +5,886 / +8,382 / +14,006 / +3,831 against returns of +20.5 / +8.9 / +14.3 / +281.5 / +5.9 / +8.4 / +14.0 / +3.8 percent.
application: The lesson is about which check to trust. Six unit tests passed on the broken version, because they all encoded MY understanding of the fee - the test asserted cost == 101 for exactly the same wrong reason the code computed it. What caught the bug was a RECONCILIATION against a number produced by a different code path: the year's return, computed by the engine's own equity curve. So for any derived measurement, the test that matters is whether it can rebuild something already known by other means, and unit tests written by the same person who wrote the function cannot supply that. Second lesson, on persistence: an inconsistency noticed once and explained away is a debt. The percentages-versus-money correction was real but incomplete, and the discrepancy was still sitting there in plain sight for a full tick.

title: FRAGILITY: five of eight years do not survive losing their best three trades - and 2022 loses on its best ONE
source: jackknife on the 3,329 round trips the shipped champion actually took (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Removing each year's largest trades from the ledger it actually produced: 2018, 2020 and 2021 still finish positive without their best three, so they are portfolios. The other five do not. 2019 survives losing one but not three. 2023, 2024 and 2025 likewise. And 2022 does not survive losing even a SINGLE trade - its +5,886 becomes -167 without the best one. Trade counts tell the same story: 541, 976, 812 and 598 in the robust or near-robust years against 34, 142, 182 and 44 in the fragile ones.
application: This is the caveat that belongs on the deployment decision the operator is about to make. Doubling the book in 2018, 2020 or 2021 doubles a portfolio; doubling it in 2022 or 2025 doubles a handful of bets, and in 2022 essentially one. So the larger book's expected gain is real - P09 measured it at +0.0308 - but its risk is concentrated precisely in the thin recent years the operator already complains about. It also puts a floor under how much any sizing change can be trusted: with 34 trades in a year, the difference between +5.9% and a loss is one position, and no amount of paired testing on eight years can make that a large sample. Worth pairing with the earlier finding that the filters are what make the strategy profitable - they remove the losing mass, but in doing so they leave some years with too few trades to be a portfolio at all.

title: The META FILTER is what starves the recent years - it cuts 29,653 chances to 155 in 2025
source: per-year opportunity funnel over every bar and symbol (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Counting how many bars survive each gate in turn - conviction band, slow trend, market breadth, meta label - shows the meta filter doing nearly all the cutting wherever it has verdicts. Its survival rate is 60.6% in 2020, then 5.5% in 2021, 1.3% in 2022, 2.4% in 2023, 1.8% in 2024 and 0.5% in 2025. In 2025 that means 29,653 candidates become 155. The other gates are comparatively mild: the band keeps 14-19%, breadth keeps 72-97%, and only the trend filter also bites in the thin years (24.6% in 2022, 38.9% in 2025 against 54-64% in the good ones). The champion runs meta_margin at 0.005, the STRICTEST of the three values the grid offers.
application: This is the direct answer to the operator's requirement of earning more EVERY year, and it relocates the problem. The thin years are thin because of opportunity count, not position size: 2022 took 34 round trips and 2025 took 44, and no amount of extra size creates a chance the filter refused to give - ten times the size still leaves 34 bets, in a year the fragility jackknife showed turns negative without its single best one. There is also an uncomfortable connection to the selection law: it rewards the WORST year, the surest way to protect a worst year is to trade less, and a strict meta filter is exactly how one trades less. So the law may be selecting a filter that is stricter than the operator's actual goal wants. Note the filter has ALREADY been measured as worth more than every sizing overlay combined - but as a binary at margins 0.0, 0.002 and 0.005, never loosened BELOW zero, where it would accept entries with a slightly negative expected net in exchange for far more of them. That is the untested direction and it is now queued as P13.

title: The funnel's first run said 2018 had ZERO tradeable bars - and the champion traded 541 times
source: correcting the opportunity funnel (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The first version of the funnel treated a MISSING meta verdict as a rejection, which put 2018 and 2019 at zero surviving bars. The champion traded 541 and 976 times in those years, so the measurement contradicted a number already known. Reading the module settled it in seconds: it vetoes only on a verdict that is present AND bad - `if verdict is not None and verdict <= margin` - so the walk-forward's earliest, train-only candidates abstain and the trade stands.
application: Third time in two days that reading the module corrected a measurement, and the first time the error announced ITSELF rather than being caught by suspicion. That is worth generalising: build every derived measurement so it can be checked against a number produced by a different code path, and look at that check first. The fee double-count was caught the same way, by a per-trade ledger that could not reproduce its own year's return. A measurement that cannot contradict anything cannot be validated either.

title: STRUCTURAL HOLE: all 44 training features are per-symbol - the net cannot see the market it trades in
source: reading FEATURE_COLUMNS during the strategic review (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The net's entire input is its own coin: multi-horizon returns, oscillators, trend strength, distances to moving averages, volatility, range position, candle geometry, flow. There is NO breadth, no BTC state, no cross-sectional rank, no market-wide volatility - every market-level judgment lives in post-hoc filters (breadth gate, meta) that the net cannot learn from. Three prior measurements cohere with this: the cross-asset horse-race lever bolted on AFTER the net was null; the meta filter, which implicitly sees market-wide outcomes, is worth more than every sizing overlay combined; and the net's edge collapses precisely in the years whose character is market-wide (the 2022 bear, the 2025 chop).
application: This is the cheapest credible GENERATION upgrade, and generation is the deep constraint: the raw rule earns no gross profit in three of the last four research years, so filter and sizing tuning are polishing a candidate stream that dries up exactly when the operator wants more. A59: append to each symbol's feature matrix the SAME causal market columns - breadth (fraction of universe in uptrend), BTC return/trend, median cross-sectional volatility, and the symbol's momentum rank within the universe. Implementation note: FEATURE_COLUMNS is pinned by the Standardizer, so old models fail loudly rather than silently - the change must go in as a flag (market_features on/off) so it can be PAIRED on the same seed, not as an edit to the tuple. If the net uses market state, regime-conditional labels (A53) follow; architecture bake-offs only after, since they are the expensive way to learn the same thing.

title: P11 LANDMARK: with a looser abort the deployment curve keeps RISING - +0.1166 at ceiling 0.90, EVERY year better
source: P11 paired on the champion genome, control exact at 0.0228 (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: The interaction test settles what P09 could only suggest. Under the old 25% abort the deployment curve collapsed above ceiling 0.50; with the cap loosened it keeps rising monotonically: ceiling 0.50 + cap 0.50 gives +0.0308 (dd 25.5%), ceiling 0.70 + cap 0.50 gives +0.0730 (dd 31.5%), ceiling 0.90 + cap 0.60 gives +0.1166 (dd 38.0%) - the largest paired delta this project has ever measured, nearly four times the previous best. No arm stops out anywhere. And the per-year rows answer the operator's requirement directly: EVERY year improves at EVERY arm - at the top arm 2018 +77 points, 2019 +42, 2020 +51, 2021 +1752, 2022 +7.0, 2023 +6.8, 2024 +11.3, 2025 +4.3. The thin years roughly double (2022 ~+5.9% to ~+12.9%, 2025 ~+3.8% to ~+8.1%) while the good years multiply.
