application: The price is stated in one number per arm: worst intra-year drawdown 25.5% / 31.5% / 38.0% against the old policy of 25%. That is the whole trade, and choosing a point on it is the operator's risk appetite - he removed the cap for exactly this. Cautions that travel with it: the curve is MONOTONE across the tested range, so the true peak may lie beyond ceiling 0.90 / cap 0.60 (P14 probes further); the thin years' gains still ride on 34-44 trades (the fragility result stands - 2022 without its best trade is negative); no arm sails its cap (38.0% vs a 0.60 cap leaves real headroom, so this is NOT the edge-sailing failure mode measured earlier); and the interaction with money_model must be MEASURED, never summed, because levers do not compose here. Two grid rows added (13 -> 15) so the autoloop now judges these configurations per net - which required adding max_drawdown to KNOWN_LEVERS first, since _row_to_kwargs would have silently stripped it and the row would have measured the wrong strategy while looking exactly right. Caught proactively this time; that trap has now appeared four times.

title: OPERATOR CRITERION (2026-08-28): balance - if gains are proportional to drawdown, take the smallest
source: operator message on seeing the 38% figure (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Refinement of the no-hard-cap mandate, in his words: a 38% drawdown is frightening because you never know whether it stops there. Seek a balance between improvement and drawdown. If a configuration's larger drawdown produces a gain merely PROPORTIONAL to the extra risk, prefer the smallest or most balanced drawdown; accept a deep one only when it buys a DISPROPORTIONATE gain relative to the rest.
application: This converts candidate selection from a curve-reading into an EFFICIENCY test: gain per point of drawdown, computed separately for typical years and for the moonshot year because 2021 dominates any mean. Applied to P11 immediately: typical-year gains scale at a flat ~1.5-1.7pp of yearly return per 1pp of drawdown across the whole deployment curve - proportional, so by his rule the deep end is NOT justified by them. money_model 0.5 is the outlier at ~4.0pp per 1pp - disproportionately efficient, so it belongs in any operating point. What the deep end buys disproportionately is only the moonshot year (2021: +237pp -> +780pp -> +1752pp super-linearly), which is a risk-appetite luxury, not a requirement of the every-year goal. Standing changes: every future report states the efficiency column alongside return and drawdown, and the taper (dd_sizer) rises in priority because it is the one mechanism aimed at keeping the gain while cutting the realised drawdown - exactly the balance he asks for. His fear is also technically well-founded and stays in reports: a measured max drawdown is a backtest statistic, the true tail is deeper, and this repository measured that configs sailing their limit generalise worse.

title: P13 REFUTED loosening the filter - GENERATION is now the PROVEN constraint
source: P13 paired on the champion genome, control exact, no inert arms (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: Loosening the meta filter loses monotonically and badly: margin 0.0 gives -0.1369, margin -0.005 gives -0.2365 with two mandate stops, and off entirely gives -0.2481 with FOUR years stopping out. Every judged thin year worsens at every loosening except a single cell (2024 at margin 0.0, +15.3pp - noise against the rest of its column). Exposure RISES from 5.49% to 12.88% while returns collapse, which is the third independent demonstration that more exposure via WORSE trades loses (trend_soft, extra position slots, now the filter).
application: This closes the filtering question and promotes a suspicion to a proof. The thin years are thin because the NET produces no profitable candidates there - the raw rule already showed no gross profit in 2022/23/25, and now we know the filter's rejections were correct, not conservative. Three consequences. The GENERATION line is the priority: P15 (market-state features) runs next, and A53 (regime-conditional labels) after it. The deployment/sizing work stands as the only measured way to lift the thin years today (+7pp in 2022 at the deep end, +2pp at the balanced end), because it multiplies the GOOD trades the filter keeps. And the operator's balance criterion sharpens the program further: P14's deep-end probe (ceiling 1.0) is demoted - typical-year gains are proportional to drawdown, so the deep end is a moonshot luxury - while P12's taper is promoted to the top, since keeping the gain at lower realised drawdown is exactly the balanced formula he asked for.

title: P12: the drawdown taper keeps a third of the cliff gain at HALF the drawdown - and beats money 0.5 on efficiency
source: P12 paired, control exact 0.0228, both seeds agree (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-28)
summary: ceiling 0.90 + dd_sizer 1.0 (Grossman-Zhou taper against the 25pct reference): +0.0358 at 21.6pct maxDD, vs P11 cliff c0.90/cap0.60 +0.1166 at 38.0pct. Per pp of drawdown ADDED over baseline (+0.9pp) the taper yields ~4x what the deployment curve yields - the second efficiency outlier after money 0.5 (+0.0228 for +1.5pp). dd_sizer alone: -0.0080 but dd 20.7->14.7 (a pure drawdown-reducer). Taper 2.0 REFUTED (-0.0150): tapering too early starves the rallies - dose matters.
application: The operator balance criterion has a new best point: taper 1.0 at ceiling 0.90. Open question MEASURED next (never assumed): composition with money 0.5 on the shipped net. If they compose, the adoption candidate becomes c0.90+taper+money; the sealed look happens once, at adoption.

title: Fourth composition failure: taper + money 0.5 breaks all-positive on the shipped net
source: taper_yearly.py on shipped champion signals, research years (2026-08-28)
summary: On the shipped net: taper alone +0.0753 all-positive; taper + money 0.5 = +0.0625 with 2025 NEGATIVE (-0.5pct) despite CAGR 67.5 (2021 +1699). Both levers multiply exposure into the same trades; in the weakest year the doubled sizing turns a +2 year into a loss. ALSO: P12 ranked taper above money on fresh paired nets, but on the SHIPPED champion the balanced config (money+c0.50+cap0.50, +0.1095) stays far ahead - lever rankings are NET-DEPENDENT; adoption decisions must be measured on the artifact that ships.
application: Balanced (money 0.5 + c0.50 + cap0.50) remains the adoption candidate. Taper stays valuable as a per-net lever for the autoloop grid (it won on fresh nets), and dd_sizer alone remains the cheapest drawdown-reducer if the operator ever wants dd cut at small cost.

title: P16: labels that certify tradability taught the net WORSE entries - honesty about survival is not information about timing
source: P16 train_ab, baseline reconciliation exact (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-29)
summary: Triple-barrier labels with the books own exits: -0.2318 mean, both seeds deeply negative, two mandate stops. Mechanism: path-survival is a property of the FORWARD WINDOW, not of the entry bar - it approves mid-swing and quiet-chop bars equally, so the positive class stops meaning a swing starts here. The zigzag labels, for all their path-blindness, encode exactly the start-of-move timing the band rule then trades.
application: Label experiments must preserve the timing semantics: refinements should INTERSECT with swing-start (or raise min_gain to swing scale), never replace it wholesale. More broadly: after P13/P15/P16, single-lever generation changes look exhausted at current dose - the remaining irons change the LEARNER (A61 committee) or the TIMEFRAME (A62), not the target.

title: P14: at the deep end on fresh nets, ceiling x money COMPOSES (+0.1468 @ 44.1pct dd) and the curve flattens past ceiling 0.90
source: P14 paired, control exact, seeds agree (system 06 R&D loop, 2026-08-29)
summary: c0.90/cap0.60+money0.5: +0.1468, EVERY year better than either lever alone (2019 +0.699, 2022 +0.096, 2025 +0.068). c1.00/cap0.75: +0.1377 - beyond ceiling 0.90 the curve flattens; the tested edge was near the real edge. P11 best reproduced exactly (+0.1166). Composition is regime-dependent AND net-dependent: taper+money broke 2025 on the shipped net, ceiling+money composes on fresh nets at the deep end. Every composition must be measured in situ - no exceptions, four confirmations now.
application: The moonshot menu has a new top point for any future operator appetite: deep+money at 44pct dd. The balanced adoption candidate is unchanged (the operator called 38pct frightening). If the autoloop ever hunts the deep regime, money 0.5 belongs in those genomes.

title: P16+P17: both label surgeries refuted - generous labels + downstream meta filter beat every alternative tried
source: P16 (-0.2318) and P17 (-0.1257), baseline reconciliation exact 4x (2026-08-29)
summary: Replacing zigzag labels with path-survival destroyed timing information (P16). Intersecting - pruning only stop-doomed positives, timing preserved - ALSO lost (P17): the dip-then-recover swing starts being pruned are the very pattern the net needs to learn early-swing shapes; their tradability is the meta filters job, and it already does it (P13). Division of labor beats label purity.
application: Close the label lever. Generation irons left: A61 committee variance (inference running), A62 1h book (hindsight gate partially answered), new-information sources (the strategy.json diagnosis: everything on file derives from price, and that well looks close to dry). The 2026 fix, if it exists, most likely needs NEW INFORMATION, not new arrangements of price.

title: Operator benchmark: textbook RSI-14+MA200 (4h, untrained) loses in 6 of 9 years and does -3.9pct in 2026 vs our +1.8pct
source: rsi_ma_baseline.py, fixed parameters decided before looking, equal-weight 14 symbols, engine costs (2026-08-29)
summary: For the untrained baseline every year including 2026 is out-of-sample. It never exceeds +8.7pct (2020) and is negative in 2018/19/22/23/25/26. The system beats it everywhere, including the only year that is honest for BOTH (2026: +1.8 vs -3.9).
application: The floor is established: the complex system extracts real signal a textbook rule does not. The operator mandate stands regardless - +1.8 forward is unacceptable - but the answer to would a simple rule beat all this is measured: no. Keep this baseline as a standing benchmark row for future walk-forward comparisons.

title: P19: on genuinely unseen years the system is roughly FLAT (median -0.8%, 4 of 7 negative) - the research table was training talking
source: P19 walk-forward campaign, 7 cutoff trainings (2026-08-29)
summary: Held-out years: 2019 -0.8, 2020 -4.7, 2021 +113.4, 2022 -10.2, 2023 -13.2, 2024 +29.2, 2025 +7.6. Mean +17.3 is carried entirely by 2021; median -0.8; only 1 of 7 clears +30%. Sealed 2026's +1.8% is not an anomaly - it is exactly what this profile predicts, which is the strongest validation the instrument could have.
application: The operator was right and the number now has seven samples instead of one. Every future lever is judged on THIS column, not on research years. First target: turn the four negative held-out years positive - and note 2022/2025 traded only ~52 times each on unseen data, so the thin-year problem is a GENERATION problem there too, exactly as P13 said.

title: The extreme-fear veto is the first lever to improve the HELD-OUT median (-0.8% -> +2.0%)
source: P20 (research, paired) + walk-forward re-evaluation on P19's seven nets (2026-08-29)
summary: Held-out: median -0.8 -> +2.0, mean +17.3 -> +21.8, negative years 4/7 -> 3/7. Concentrated in active years (2019 +2.8pp, 2021 +28.4pp), exactly zero in 2022-2025 where exposure is 1-4% and there is almost nothing to veto.
application: Two lessons. (1) Non-price information works where price-derived levers all failed - keep mining that seam (funding parked, on-chain untried). (2) The thin years are immune to ANY entry filter by arithmetic: with 1-4% exposure there is nothing to refuse. Their fix must create trades (generation), not remove them - which is now proven twice, by P13 from the loosening side and by this from the tightening side.

title: A remembered rule failed twice; the runner now publishes the code fingerprint it is executing
source: P05 (2026-08-27) and P21 crashing twice on an already-fixed bug (2026-08-29)
summary: Python binds imports at process start, so a file fixed on disk changes nothing until a restart. This lab recorded that rule after P05 lost a whole experiment to it - and then I broke the same rule myself: I fixed the train_ab collision, requeued P21, and let the OLD process run it, so it failed identically. Rules that live only in memory are not controls.
application: The runner hashes its own source at import and stamps CODE_FINGERPRINT into every heartbeat, so a result can be checked against the code that produced it and a stale process is visible rather than silent. General principle for this project: when a guard depends on someone remembering, convert it into something the system emits or refuses.

title: P21: a purged-CV embargo makes this system WORSE (-0.135 at 1 day, -0.192 at 10)
source: P21 train_ab, 2 seeds, both arms negative and dose-responsive (2026-08-30)
summary: Leakage at the train/val boundary was the first suspect for the research-vs-held-out gap P19 measured. Removing it loses monotonically: embargo 96 bars -0.1353, embargo 960 -0.1922, with drawdown rising 30.5 -> 35.7 in both arms. Seeds disagree in sign on the 1-day arm (+0.054 / -0.054), so the honest reading of that cell is 'noisy and not positive'; the 10-day arm is negative on both.
application: The generalisation gap is NOT boundary leakage - it is the ordinary cost of trading an unseen regime, which the walk-forward instrument now measures directly. Stop hunting leakage in the split and keep judging on held-out years. Practical note: the embargo also DELETES training data at the exact end of the training window - the most recent, most relevant bars - which is a plausible mechanism for the loss and a reason to leave it at 0 here.

title: P22: averaging three nets still loses (-0.1587) even after the mechanism A43 blamed was removed
source: P22 train_ab, 2 seeds, on the adopted shipping config (2026-08-30)
summary: A43 refuted bagging and blamed the band selector, which has since been pinned. Re-tested on that fixed ground, bagging still loses -0.1587 with drawdown up 30.5 -> 32.7. So the original diagnosis was incomplete: the harm is not (only) selector variance. Plausible remaining mechanism, consistent with the ensemble's own arithmetic: averaging pulls extreme convictions toward the middle, and this book trades ONLY the extremes (enter 0.75 of a bagged mean is a far rarer and different event than 0.75 of a single net) - a hesitant voice drags a confident one below the threshold to act, which is exactly what the A32 tree post-mortem said about averaging opinions.
application: Variance reduction by averaging is closed for this architecture - twice now, under different conditions. If seed variance is to be tamed, it must be done by SELECTION (the median-of-reseeds promotion rule already in place) rather than by blending signals.

title: The wide candidate's 2026 was +35.1%, -21.1% and -43.5% across three seeds - the reseed rule earned its keep
source: champion_wide, three seeds, sealed readout after research selection (2026-08-30)
summary: Seed 77101 read +35.1% on the forward year - the best this system has produced and above the operator's 30% line. The other two read -21.1% and -43.5%. Median -21.1%. Research selection had ALREADY rejected the candidate (median score +0.0037 against a +0.0972 bar, and no seed green in every year), so nothing was shipped; but had the promotion rule been a single draw, we would have shipped a book whose typical forward year loses a fifth of the account.
application: Two things. (1) The median-of-reseeds rule is not bureaucracy - it is the only thing standing between an exciting number and a disaster, and this is its clearest demonstration to date. (2) The wide universe carries MUCH higher seed variance than the narrow one (spread 78pp on the forward year), which is itself evidence about dilution: with 24 candidates the top-2 pick depends far more on where a particular net happened to land. Any future wide champion must be judged on the median, never the best draw.

title: The breadth thesis is closed in all four directions - and the seasoning fix is inert exactly where it matters
source: A37, A40, A66/ARCH-0003, A68, ARCH-0004 seasoning sweep (2026-08-30)
summary: Trade wide (A37): refuted. Train wide, trade narrow (A40): refuted. Train AND trade wide (ARCH-0003): median sealed 2026 -21.1% across three seeds, research median +0.0037 vs a +0.0972 bar. Narrow net shopping a wide market (A68): -22.8% and -29.7% in the 2019/2020 held-out years against -0.8% and -4.7% narrow. Wide plus the causal seasoning gate (ARCH-0004): the gate does help the early years - worst research year -3.9% -> ~0.0%, median score +0.0037 -> +0.0326 - but no seed turns green in every year, it stays far below the bar, and the sealed 2026 readouts are IDENTICAL to ARCH-0003 because by 2026 every symbol is older than the gate. The repair cannot reach the year that counts.
application: Stop paying for breadth on this architecture. The mechanism is now understood rather than merely observed: with only two slots, a bigger candidate pool does not diversify - it makes the top-2 pick depend on where a particular net happened to land, which shows up as a 78pp seed spread on the forward year. If breadth is ever revisited it needs a structurally different book (many more concurrent positions, or per-symbol calibration), not a wider list bolted onto a two-position book.
